Real-life outcome data remain limited. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis of the German Stroke Registry-Endovascular Treatment comparing extensive (ASPECTS 0-2) and large infarcts (ASPECTS 3-5) in patients with anterior-circulation occlusion and EVT.

title: [Non-anatomic Bypass for Severe Brachiocephalic Artery Stenosis due to Dissecting Aneurysm After Total Arch Aortic Replacement for Stanford Type A Acute Aortic Dissection:Report of a Case].
abstract: Dissecting brachiocephalic artery aneurysm after total arch aortic replacement poses a risk of postoperative cerebral infarction, yet no consensus exists regarding optimal management. Treatment decisions rely on the patient's condition, degree of true lumen stenosis, and lesion characteristics. We report a case of a dissecting brachiocephalic aneurysm with severe true lumen stenosis following surgery for Stanford type A acute aortic dissection. A 70-year-old man was transferred to our hospital with acute aortic dissection and multiple right-hemispheric cerebral infarctions and underwent emergency total arch replacement. On postoperative day nine, contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed progressive false lumen expansion with significant true lumen compression. To prevent further cerebral ischemia, a left axillary-right common carotid artery non-anatomic bypass was performed. The patient gradually recovered left upper limb function and was transferred for rehabilitation on postoperative day 27.

Treatment decisions rely on the patient's condition, degree of true lumen stenosis, and lesion characteristics. We report a case of a dissecting brachiocephalic aneurysm with severe true lumen stenosis following surgery for Stanford type A acute aortic dissection.

title: [Aortic Root Replacement for a Left Sinus of Valsalva Aneurysm Complicated by Ascending Aortic Dissection:Report of a Case].
abstract: We report a case of a left sinus of Valsalva aneurysm (SVA) complicated by ascending aortic dissection (AAD). A 37-year-old man presented to our hospital with worsening leg edema and was diagnosed with heart failure due to severe aortic regurgitation (AR). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) and transesophageal echocardiography revealed the presence of an AAD and a left SVA. After medical treatment for heart failure, the patient underwent aortic root replacement. The postoperative course was favorable. The combination of SVA and AAD in a young patient is extremely rare and may lead to delayed diagnosis. Therefore, thorough investigation of the underlying cause is essential, particularly in young patients presenting with heart failure or AR.

title: Nomogram for Postoperative Permanent Neurologic Dysfunction Following Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Surgery: A Multicentral Retrospective Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Permanent neurologic dysfunction (PND) often complicates following surgery for acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) and is strongly correlated with unfavorable outcomes. Consequently, developing an effective diagnostic method to identify high-risk patients is of considerable importance. METHODS: This retrospective study, covering 2022 to 2024 across two centers, ultimately included 117 ATAAD patients with Supra-Aortic Branch Vessel (SABV) dissection from our center (2022-2023) as the training set and 52 ATAAD patients with SABV dissection from a secondary center (2024) as the validation set. We used logistic regression to identify predictors and developed a nomogram, which was assessed using the area under the ROC curve, calibration and decision curve analysis. External validation was conducted using the validation set. RESULTS: In this study, 169 cases were finally collected (117 in the training set and 52 in the validation set), of whom 64 patients developed postoperative PND. Four risk factors were identified: brachiocephalic trunk dissection at the bifurcation plane, chronic kidney disease, age over 50, and cross-clamp duration over 168 min. The AUC was 0.809 for the training set and 0.736 for the validation set. The nomogram model demonstrated acceptable predictive performance, and decision curve analysis potential clinical utility for predicting postoperative PND risk for thresholds of 1%-90% in the training set and 3%-75% in the validation set. CONCLUSIONS: This study developed and validated a predictive model for assessing the risk of postoperative PND in patients undergoing ATAAD surgery, which may assist clinicians in individualized risk assessment.

title: Development of Aortic Stents from Open Surgery to Endovascular Therapy: A Brazilian Contribution to the Treatment of Aortic Diseases.
abstract: The treatment of aortic diseases has undergone profound transformation over the last decades, with the progressive incorporation of endovascular techniques either replacing or complementing conventional open surgical repair. The development of aortic stents represents one of the most significant milestones in this transition. This article reviews the historical, experimental, and clinical evolution of aortic stents, with emphasis on pioneering Brazilian contributions, including the experimental phase in animal models, the first clinical applications in aortic dissection, and the role of the national industry in the development and dissemination of these technologies. The impact of these innovations on contemporary cardiovascular surgical practice and future perspectives are also discussed.

title: State of Art of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for the Treatment of Aortic Stenosis in Low-Risk Patients: A Perspective on Brazilian Contributions and Implementation Challenges.
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has profoundly changed the management of severe aortic stenosis (AS), evolving from a treatment reserved for inoperable and high-risk patients to an established therapeutic option across a wide surgical risk spectrum. Although the expansion of TAVI indications has been largely supported by randomized clinical trials conducted in high-income countries, real-world experience and technological contributions from distinct healthcare systems are increasingly relevant. Brazil has played a significant role in the early adoption, structured implementation, and clinical evaluation of TAVI in Latin America. Since the first procedures performed in 2008, Brazilian centers have developed Heart Team models, contributed to national and regional registries, and generated real-world evidence demonstrating procedural safety and effectiveness comparable to international benchmarks, despite the presence of resource limitations and a higher prevalence of complex clinical and anatomical scenarios. The incorporation of TAVI into the Brazilian public health system in 2022 marked a major milestone in expanding access to minimally invasive therapy for patients with severe AS. In parallel, Brazilian scientific societies have adapted international guideline recommendations to local practice, supporting evidence-based patient selection across different surgical risk categories. Notably, Brazil has also emerged as a developer of locally engineered transcatheter valve technologies, highlighting its transition from a technology consumer to an active contributor in the field of structural heart disease. This review summarizes the historical evolution, national experience, clinical outcomes, guideline integration, technological innovation, and health economic considerations of TAVI in Brazil.

title: Snare-Assisted Traction Technique for Renal Artery Reconstruction in Endovascular Repair of Complex Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: Renal artery (RA) reconstruction during complex endovascular aortic repair often fails in hostile anatomy because of inadequate guidewire support. We describe snare-assisted traction (SAT), a novel endovascular bailout technique using conventional off-the-shelf devices. By combining distal snare traction with a long femoral sheath, SAT shifts target vessel reconstruction from simple wire guidance to sheath-based structural support. This provides robust stability for wire exchange and stent delivery without requiring specialized, unavailable tools or high-morbidity open conversion. Among 12 patients with severe RA angulation, ostial stenosis, or sac origin, SAT achieved 100% technical success without procedural complications. At median 6-month follow-up, all reconstructed RAs remained patent with stable renal function. SAT offers a safe, reproducible, and universally accessible solution for hostile target vessel access, significantly enhancing the feasibility and clinical safety of complex endovascular repair.

title: An anatomy-aware spatio-temporal generative extrapolation network for distal ascending aorta restoration in standard echocardiographic views.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), the standard parasternal long-axis (PLAX) view enables reliable evaluation of the aortic valve and aortic root. Owing to the limited field of view of the ultrasound probe and rib-window occlusion, the distal ascending aorta (AA) is frequently truncated, compromising the diagnosis of aortic aneurysm and dilation. PURPOSE: We aim to address the incomplete visualization of the distal AA in standard PLAX views. By aggregating fragmented anatomical features intermittently visible in adjacent frames, we enhance the clarity of vessel wall edges and generate the distal AA structure, thereby completing the missing AA imagery in standard PLAX views. MATERIALS AND METHODS: ± Δ = 0.2 cm We retrospectively collected 1160 TTE videos from Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital (August 2022 - December 2024), all showing complete AA anatomy. After de-identification, 1059 cases were randomly split into training/validation/test sets (6:2:2), and 101 cases were reserved for observer agreement experiments. An additional 152 videos from three different device models (EPIQ CVX, GE Voluson E10, Resona A20T) formed an external validation set. Two training data types were constructed: (i) dual-view synchronous data - a standard PLAX sequence and an AO-PLAX sequence acquired after a cranial probe shift, phase-matched at end diastole (ED); and (ii) locally masked data - the distal AA region was masked, forcing the model to infer missing anatomy from left-side context. Input sequences of five frames (ED2) were extracted. The proposed Spatio-Temporal Ascending-Aorta generative adversarial network (STAA-GAN) first aligns adjacent frames using an Edge Boosted Feature Alignment (EBFA) module with multi-stage modulated deformable convolutions. A channel-wise fusion strategy then aggregates temporally aligned features. The fused representation is fed into a Swin-UNet generator enhanced with a Strip based Cross window Prediction (SCP) module to capture long-range structural dependencies. Training employs a composite loss including pixel reconstruction, feature reconstruction, texture consistency, relativistic average least-squares GAN (RaLSGAN), temporal coherence, and structure-aware terms, with data-dependent weighting. Statistical analyzes included Bland-Altman, Passing-Bablok regression, paired t-tests with Cohen's d, Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, and two one-sided tests (TOST,). RESULTS: α 1 = 0.00417 ≤ 0.01 ± 0.13 Δ = 0.2 p < 0.001 0.913 0.045 ± p < 0.001 d < 0.2 STAA-GAN achieved the best image-quality values among the compared methods, with peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) = 22.51 dB, structural similarity index (SSIM) = 0.7574, multi-scale structural similarity index (MS-SSIM) = 0.8598, and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) = 0.1758. All 12 pairwise comparisons (SRN, IOH, and U-Transformer versus STAA-GAN, designated as the reference group) remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (), with absolute effect sizes ranging from 0.255 to 3.439. The per-frame inference time was 203 ms. In clinical consistency validation, the mean difference between measurements on generated and original images was cm with 95% limits of agreement within cm; TOST with cm confirmed clinical equivalence for all comparisons (). The segmentation Dice coefficient on generated images averagedacross five cross-validation folds. External validation on three different ultrasound devices (Philips, GE, Mindray) maintained consistent equivalence (TOST, Cohen's). These results demonstrate that STAA-GAN produces clinically interchangeable distal ascending aorta images with high fidelity and real-time feasibility. CONCLUSIONS: STAA-GAN enables extrapolation of the missing distal ascending aorta in standard PLAX views, achieving improved image quality and clinically equivalent diameter measurements on both internal and external validation datasets. These findings support its potential for assisting distal ascending aorta assessment in routine echocardiography.

title: A comparison of the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants with low molecular weight heparin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: AIMS: To evaluate differences in the efficacy and safety of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) used for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after elective total hip arthroplasty (THA). METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis reviewed MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from conception to 13 December 2025, for any randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the efficacy (VTE risk) and safety (bleeding risk) of LMWH and DOACs after elective THA. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) of VTE, bleeding, reoperation, and mortality risks were assessed. RESULTS: A total of 22 RCTs involving 28,112 participants were included. The risk of VTE in the DOAC group was lower compared with the LMWH group (OR 0.62 (95% CI 0.47 to 0.82); p = 0.002), driven by a reduction in deep vein thrombosis (DVT) risk (OR 0.60 (95% CI 0.42 to 0.86); p = 0.008). The findings remained consistent in the subgroup analysis restricted to anticoagulants and dosages licensed for use in the UK. Overall bleeding risk was higher in the DOAC group (OR 1.19 (95% CI 1.03 to 1.38); p = 0.023), but no difference was seen when comparing only UK-licensed anticoagulants and doses (OR 1.06 (95% CI 0.95 to 1.18); p = 0.279). Reoperation risk (OR 1.21 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.93); p = 0.351) and mortality (OR 1.03 (95% CI 0.46 to 2.33); p = 0.937) did not differ between groups. CONCLUSION: DOACs reduce the risk of VTE and DVT following elective THA compared with LMWH without increasing bleeding risk, for UK-licensed agents and doses. Switching to DOACs could save the NHS £8.6 million per year. New clinical trials are needed to compare the safety and efficacy of UK-licensed DOACs and LWMH with modern postoperative rehabilitation protocols.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis reviewed MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from conception to 13 December 2025, for any randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the efficacy (VTE risk) and safety (bleeding risk) of LMWH and DOACs after elective THA. title: [Efficacy of percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy combined with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt for acute non-cirrhotic portal vein thrombosis].
abstract: Objective: Methods: Results: Conclusions: M t t CI CI HR CI P HR CI P HR CI P P vs. t P To evaluate the efficacy of percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy combined with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (PMT-TIPS) in patients with acute non-cirrhotic portal vein thrombosis (NCPVT).This is a retrospective case series study. The clinical data of 61 patients with acute NCPVT who underwent PMT combined with TIPS at Department of Endovascular Surgery, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University between June 2017 and June 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. There were 39 males and 22 females, with an age ((IQR)) of 49.0 (24.5)years (range:21 to 73 years). Paired sample-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test were used to compare liver volume and biochemical parameters before treatment and at 1 year after treatment. Independent sample-test was used to compare changes in liver volume between patients with different stent patency statuses. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate stent patency and symptom recurrence. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to analyze the factors associated with stent occlusion.Among the 61 patients, 7 (11.5%) died during hospitalization and 5 (8.2%) died within 30 days after discharge, most commonly due to bowel necrosis. The remaining 49 patients were followed up for 43 (34) months (range:4 to 94 months). During follow-up, stent occlusion occurred in 35 patients (71.4%), with a median primary patency of 13.0 months (95%: 7.3 to 18.7 months). Among the 35 patients with primary stent occlusion, 21 developed symptom recurrence, whereas symptom recurrence occurred in 4 of the 14 patients with sustained patency. Ten patients with stent occlusion underwent stent recanalization, with a median secondary patency of 21.0 months (95%: 16.8 to 25.2 months). Univariate Cox regression analysis showed that myeloproliferative neoplasms (=3.08, 95%: 1.48 to 6.42,=0.003) and dual-stent implantation (=2.26, 95%: 1.09 to 4.70,=0.036) were associated with an increased risk of stent occlusion; multivariate Cox regression further revealed that only myeloproliferative neoplasms (=2.75, 95%: 1.31 to 5.78,=0.008) was an independent risk factor. At one year post-procedure, inflammatory and coagulation markers improved, total liver volume decreased compared with baseline (=0.005), and the reduction in liver volume was greater in patients with patent stents than in those with stent occlusion ((-215.6±205.5)cm³(-3.5±236.5) cm³,=-3.505,=0.001).In patients with acute NCPVT, the PMT-TIPS technique is feasible, but long-term stent patency is limited. This technique can be used as a rescue strategy rather than a definitive treatment.

title: [Dominant false lumen flow and abnormally high shear stress: a hemodynamic analysis of multichanneled aortic dissection].
abstract: Objective: Methods: Results: Conclusions: To explore the hemodynamic characteristics of multichanneled aortic dissection (MCAD).This is a retrospective cohort study. Patients with acute uncomplicated Stanford-type B aortic dissection who presented at Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University between January 2019 and December 2023 were enrolled. Patients were diagnosed as having either double-channeled aortic dissection (DCAD) or MCAD based on preoperative standardized computed-tomography angiography (CTA). Centered on 4 MCAD cases with preprocedural death, 4 non-preprocedural-death MCAD patients and 4 non-preprocedural-death DCAD patients with balanced baseline characteristics, complete preoperative CTA datasets and well-defined outcomes were matched, yielding a total of 12 male patients. The ages of patients in preprocedural-death MCAD group, non-preprocedural-death MCAD group and non-preprocedural- death DCAD group were (62.0±5.7) years (range:54 to 66 years), (61.5±5.8) years (range:54 to 67 years) and (61.3±8.1) years (range:52 to 71 years), respectively. Using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and patient-specific aortic models, preoperative hemodynamic indices were quantitatively analyzed, including blood flow velocity, pressure distribution, flow distribution, wall shear stress (WSS) and time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS).Hemodynamic analyses revealed a stepwise decreasing trend of false lumen (FL) flow rate across the three groups. The preoperative death MCAD group exhibited a significantly higher FL flow ((62.81±7.59)ml/s (range: 56.29 to 73.78 ml/s)) than the non-preoperative death MCAD group ((24.84±9.25)ml/s (range: 17.23 to 36.84 ml/s)) and the non-preoperative death DCAD group ((11.86±5.62)ml/s (range: 6.72 to 19.84 ml/s)). The intergroup variation patterns of FL flow ratio and maximum FL TAWSS were highly consistent. The preoperative death MCAD group yielded values of 0.77±0.16 (range: 0.56 to 0.93) and (34.44±6.50)Pa (range: 27.54 to 41.38 Pa),which were elevated compared with the non-preoperative death MCAD group (0.44±0.17(range: 0.33 to 0.70), (15.46±7.75)Pa (range: 6.69 to 25.01 Pa)) and the non-preoperative death DCAD group (0.22±0.11(range: 0.14 to 0.37), (20.80±7.34)Pa (range: 15.23 to 31.60 Pa)),whereas no obvious disparities were observed between the latter two groups. In addition,the maximum FL WSS in the preoperative death MCAD group reached (125.76±26.57)Pa (range: 87.55 to 147.91 Pa),markedly exceeding that of the non-preoperative death MCAD group ((64.89±30.45)Pa (range: 28.62 to 102.40 Pa)) and the non-preoperative death DCAD group ((91.15±28.16)Pa (range: 61.51 to 126.41 Pa)).Elevated FL flow and abnormally high shear stress may correlate with poor outcomes in patients with MCAD,and these parameters could serve as potential biomechanical biomarkers. CFD simulation can act as an auxiliary tool to identify high-risk aortic dissection patients,which helps refine clinical management and facilitate individualized precision treatment for MCAD.

Patients with acute uncomplicated Stanford-type B aortic dissection who presented at Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University between January 2019 and December 2023 were enrolled. Patients were diagnosed as having either double-channeled aortic dissection (DCAD) or MCAD based on preoperative standardized computed-tomography angiography (CTA).

title: [Value of a CT angiography-based deep learning model for differentiating SVS grade Ⅱ and grade Ⅲ blunt thoracic aortic injury: a retrospective multicenter staged study].
abstract: Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: CI To develop a segmentation-guided multitask deep learning model for Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) grades Ⅰ to Ⅳ classification of blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI) and validate its clinical utility for differentiating SVS grades Ⅱ and Ⅲ.This is a retrospective case series study. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) data were collected from 317 patients with BTAI at 12 hospitals in China, including the First Medical Center of Chinese People's Liberation Army General Hospital, West China Hospital of Sichuan University, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University, and other local hospitals, between January 2006 and May 2026. The cohort included 258 male and 59 female patients, with an age of (54.8±15.3) years (range:16 to 92 years). The 253-patient development cohort was divided using a patient-level random split stratified by SVS injury grade and source center at an approximate ratio of 8∶2 into a training set of 202 patients and an internal validation set of 51 patients. The 64 BTAI cases from the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University were locked in advance as an independent external test set. The model consisted of a shared encoder, a lesion-segmentation branch, and a mask-guided classification branch. The primary outcomes were the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and grade Ⅲ sensitivity for differentiating SVS grade Ⅱ (intramural hematoma) from grade Ⅲ (pseudoaneurysm) in the external test set. Secondary outcomes included segmentation, automated measurements, and offline reader-study results.The internal validation set covered SVS grades Ⅰ to Ⅳ, with an overall grading accuracy of 92.2% (47/51) and a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.919. The external test set included 31 SVS grade Ⅱ (intramural hematoma) cases and 33 SVS grade Ⅲ (pseudoaneurysm) cases. The model had an AUC of 0.968 (95%:0.924 to 0.996), an accuracy of 92.2% (59/64), grade Ⅲ sensitivity of 93.9% (31/33), and grade Ⅱ specificity of 90.3% (28/31); two grade Ⅲ cases were misclassified as grade Ⅱ. The automated segmentation success rate was 96.9% (62/64), the overall lesion Dice similarity coefficient was 0.872±0.072 (range:0.46 to 0.99), and model inference time per case was (15.4±2.4) s (range:10.8 to 22.6 s). In the fixed-sequence reader study, six junior physicians had higher grade Ⅱ/Ⅲ accuracy and grade Ⅲ sensitivity and shorter interpretation times during the artificial intelligence-assisted phase than during the unaided phase.The segmentation-guided CTA deep learning model developed in this study performed BTAI lesion segmentation, SVS grading, and measurement of key morphologic parameters, and maintained good discrimination between SVS grades Ⅱ and Ⅲ in the independent external test set. Model assistance may help reduce missed grade Ⅲ cases by junior physicians and shorten interpretation time, thereby supporting standardized imaging assessment of BTAI.

title: [Is there still a role for manual deployment techniques in the era of fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair? Normative boundaries and practical value in the management of hostile aortic landing zones].
abstract: Standard endovascular aortic repair has been widely used for the treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysms and selected complex aortic diseases because of its minimally invasive nature, rapid recovery, and favorable perioperative safety profile. However, in hostile aortic landing zones characterized by a short neck, severe angulation, conical neck configuration, mural thrombus, or circumferential calcification, standard endovascular repair remains associated with inadequate proximal apposition, type Ⅰ endoleak, endograft migration, and secondary intervention. Manual deployment techniques, including the push-up technique, reverse slider technique, Kabedon technique, and stepwise controlled deployment, may improve endograft axial alignment, proximal edge positioning, and local wall apposition to some extent; however, their role is mainly limited to optimization of the deployment process and cannot replace the principle of a durable sealing zone. This review summarizes the anatomical characteristics of hostile aortic landing zones, the mechanisms and clinical evidence of manual deployment techniques, the standardized value of fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair and physician-modified endografts, adjunctive fixation and intraoperative bailout techniques, and application scenarios in emergency repair of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms. The aim is to provide a practical reference for rational selection between optimized deployment of standard endografts and complex sealing-zone reconstruction in complex endovascular aortic repair.
englishSummary: Standard endovascular aortic repair has been widely used for the treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysms and selected complex aortic diseases because of its minimally invasive nature, rapid recovery, and favorable perioperative safety profile. However, in hostile aortic landing zones characterized by a short neck, severe angulation, conical neck configuration, mural thrombus, or circumferential calcification, standard endovascular repair remains associated with inadequate proximal apposition, type Ⅰ endoleak, endograft migration, and secondary intervention. Manual deployment techniques, including the push-up technique, reverse slider technique, Kabedon technique, and stepwise controlled deployment, may improve endograft axial alignment, proximal edge positioning, and local wall apposition to some extent; however, their role is mainly limited to optimization of the deployment process and cannot replace the principle of a durable sealing zone.

title: [Technical considerations and advances in distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia of the lower extremities].
abstract: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) represents the end stage of lower extremity arterial disease and is associated with high rates of disability and mortality. With the rapid advancement of endovascular techniques, an "endovascular-first" strategy has become widely adopted. However, for patients with complex, long-segment, heavily calcified, diffuse, inflammatory lesions, or those with repeated endovascular failure, distal bypass surgery remains an indispensable option for limb salvage. The success of distal bypass depends not only on advanced surgical expertise but also on appropriate patient selection, accurate assessment of inflow and outflow tracts, optimal conduit choice, and meticulous perioperative management. Based on recent international guidelines and clinical evidence, this review focuses on key technical aspects of distal bypass, including inflow selection, target artery assessment, conduit selection, graft tunneling, distal anastomosis, intraoperative flow assessment, postoperative antithrombotic therapy and wound management. It also discusses the appropriate role of these techniques in the comprehensive treatment of CLTI based on recent evidence-based medical findings. In addition, emerging developments such as alternative conduits, and gene/cell therapy are discussed, aiming to provide insights into optimizing revascularization strategies for patients with CLTI.

title: [From critical evaluation based on the gold standard to precision full-process management: advances in the diagnosis and treatment framework for aortic arch artery pathologies].
abstract: Supra-aortic arch artery diseases, including lesions of the carotid,subclavian,and vertebral arteries,represent major causes of cerebral and upper extremity ischemia. The diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for these conditions are undergoing a profound transformation-from conventional open surgery toward minimally invasive endovascular treatment,and further to individualized precision medicine. Recent advances in imaging assessment have substantially improved lesion characterization and risk stratification. The iterative evolution of endovascular devices has enhanced procedural safety. Meanwhile,several topics have become research hotspots,the evidence-based comparison between transcarotid artery revascularization and transfemoral carotid stenting;the renewed pathophysiological understanding of subclavian steal syndrome and vertebral artery diseases;and the construction of individualized treatment decision-making frameworks. Nevertheless,current clinical practice still faces challenges such as controversies over optimal surgical approaches,insufficient prevention and management of complications,and a lack of robust long-term outcome data. From the perspective of vascular surgery,this article systematically reviews recent advances in endovascular devices,surgical techniques,and treatment concepts,aiming to provide front-line clinicians with up-to-date,practical,and actionable insights into the management of supra-aortic arch artery diseases.

title: [A brief discussion on the progress and development directions of clinical research in vascular surgery].
abstract: Vascular surgery has experienced rapid development over the past three decades. With the application of minimally invasive and interventional techniques in the diagnosis and treatment of vascular diseases, clinical research and technological innovation in vascular surgery have expanded significantly. As populations aging accelerates globally-including in China-and the number of patients with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease within the existing healthcare system becomes increasingly evident. The future of vascular surgery will center on three core principles: minimization, precision, and intelligence. By integrating breakthroughs in basic science, engineering, and artificial intelligence, clinical translation will be accelerated. The discipline will shift from "disease treatment" to "health management", and from a "surgery-centered" single model to a "patient-centered" integrated approach model. Future developments will further incorporate artificial intelligence, big data models, precision medicine, more advanced and comprehensive minimally invasive technologies, enhancing multidisciplinary collaboration and preventive care. These advancements are expected to significantly improve diagnostic accuracy, treatment outcomes, and quality of life for patients with vascular diseases.

title: Outcomes post-thrombectomy in children: A multi-site assessment of a new non-lytic endovascular device combined with anticoagulation for management of adolescents with extensive acute lower limb deep vein thrombosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Adolescents who develop extensive lower extremity deep venous thrombosis (DVT) are at high-risk for adverse outcomes including post-thrombotic syndrome (PTS) with anticoagulation alone. New mechanical thrombectomy devices, such as the ClotTriever® device, have been reported to reduce PTS in adults, however, there is limited data in adolescents with lower extremity DVT. AIM: To assess outcomes of adolescents post-mechanical thrombectomy with a ClotTriever® device for extensive lower extremity DVT in a multisite Canadian cohort. METHODS: Adolescents (age 10- < 18 years) who underwent mechanical thrombectomy with a ClotTriever® device for extensive lower extremity DVT between 01/2023-03/2026 at 5 Canadian centres were reviewed retrospectively. Data collected included demographics, DVT symptoms/risks, imaging, anticoagulation, procedure details and bleeding (major and clinically relevant non-major (CRNM)). Outcomes on imaging and PTS assessments (CAPTSure© score) were completed at 6 and/or ≥12 months post-thrombectomy. RESULTS: Twenty-one patients were identified with 20/21 undergoing thrombectomy <2 weeks from symptom onset. 20/21 had follow-up imaging after anticoagulation therapy with 12/20 showing full resolution of thrombus. No patients had major or CRNM bleeding post-thrombectomy even with intensive periprocedural anticoagulation. All patients completed PTS assessments with CAPTSure© scores at 6 and/or ≥12 months post-thrombectomy (median 12 months) with 19/21 having no PTS, 1/21 having mild PTS and 1/21 having moderate-severe PTS. CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest adolescents with extensive lower limb DVT who underwent thrombectomy with ClotTriever® in combination with anticoagulation had a high rate of thrombus resolution and a low rate of PTS. Lack of bleeding events may be an advantage over endovascular thrombolysis in this population.

title: Impact of Balloon-Expandable Valve Asymmetry on Heart Failure Post Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Fluoroscopic assessment enables immediate evaluation of transcatheter heart valve expansion during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Whether fluoroscopic asymmetric expansion of balloon-expandable valves is associated with post-TAVR heart failure (HF) remains uncertain. METHODS: Among 607 consecutive patients undergoing balloon-expandable valve-TAVR in a prospective registry, 589 were analyzed. Valve asymmetry was quantified using a fluoroscopic asymmetry index (%), defined as [(longest/shortest balloon-expandable valve height)-1]×100. The primary end point was 2-year HF hospitalization. RESULTS: P P P During follow-up, 99 patients (17%) experienced HF hospitalization. As a continuous variable, asymmetry index (%) was not independently associated with 2-year HF (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1% increase, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.98-1.06]). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated no significant linear or nonlinear association (overall=0.71;for nonlinearity=0.89), although the risk curve suggested increased HF risk beyond moderate valve asymmetry. Exploratory threshold analysis identified an asymmetry index cutoff of 7.48%. Patients above this threshold had a higher incidence of HF hospitalization than those below it (23.6% versus 15.8%; log-rank=0.043), despite comparable rates of impaired valve performance at discharge. Valve asymmetry >7.48% remained independently associated with late HF occurring beyond 30 days after TAVR (adjusted HR, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.10-2.60]). CONCLUSIONS: Fluoroscopic assessment of balloon-expandable valve expansion identified patients with marked valve asymmetry at increased risk of late HF after TAVR, despite preserved early valve performance. These findings support the potential value of intraprocedural valve geometry assessment for long-term risk stratification and warrant further investigation.

Whether fluoroscopic asymmetric expansion of balloon-expandable valves is associated with post-TAVR heart failure (HF) remains uncertain. METHODS: Among 607 consecutive patients undergoing balloon-expandable valve-TAVR in a prospective registry, 589 were analyzed.

title: Beyond Anatomy in Uncomplicated Type B Aortic Dissection: Hypoxia, Physiological Reserve, and the Next Generation of Intelligent Endovascular Devices.
abstract: Type B aortic dissection (TBAD) represents a heterogeneous disease process that cannot be fully understood through anatomy alone. Although the majority of patients initially meet current criteria for uncomplicated TBAD (uTBAD), a substantial proportion later progresses despite appearing stable during early assessment and surveillance. The mechanisms underlying this deterioration remain incompletely understood and extends beyond our current understanding of traditional anatomic high-risk criteria. This article examines impaired oxygenation and physiological reserve as potential dimensions of clinical vulnerability in uTBAD, while distinguishing their possible relevance to acute deterioration from their unproven value in predicting aortic progression or selecting patients for intervention. As such, TBAD is not simply a focal vascular event, but a disease with broader systemic and physiological implications. It also discusses how future intelligent endovascular technologies could support a more personalised approach to management by integrating embedded sensors, wireless physiological monitoring, and artificial intelligence-assisted haemodynamic analysis. Moreover, a conceptual framework is discussed in which the stent graft evolves from a purely mechanical device into an active therapeutic platform capable of physiological sensing and real-time feedback.

title: Prognostic Value of the Frailty Index in Patients with Severe Aortic Regurgitation Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty represents a multidimensional vulnerability that predicts poor outcomes in cardiovascular disease. Its prognostic value in patients with severe native aortic regurgitation (AR) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is not well defined. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether an abbreviated cumulative deficit frailty index predicts one-year all-cause mortality and to explore its interaction with N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide in this population. METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of the prospective China DVD2 multicenter cohort, 298 patients with isolated severe AR who underwent TAVR were included. Frailty was assessed preprocedurally using an abbreviated 8-9-item cumulative deficit frailty index (FI) encompassing functional, cognitive, nutritional, and clinical domains. The primary endpoint was one-year all-cause mortality. The cohort-derived FI threshold for mortality was derived using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, atrial fibrillation, and NT-proBNP were applied. Subgroup and interaction analyses were performed. RESULTS: The cohort-derived FI threshold was 0.407, classifying 32 patients as high frailty. High-FI patients exhibited greater symptom burden, higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation, larger left atrial diameter, and elevated NT-proBNP. One-year mortality was significantly higher in the high-FI group compared with low-FI patients (15.6% vs 3.4%, P = 0.010). High FI was associated with higher one-year mortality in Model 3 (HR 4.00, 95% CI 1.18-13.50; P = 0.026). No significant multiplicative or additive interaction with NT-proBNP was observed. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing TAVR for severe native aortic regurgitation, a high FI was associated with higher one-year mortality. These findings extend prior evidence on the prognostic implications of frailty to this understudied population.

title: Comparison of Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters versus Central Venous Catheters in a Medical Intensive Care Unit: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients in medical intensive care units (MICUs) often require prolonged intravenous therapy, making optimal catheter selection critical. While central venous catheters (CVCs) remain common, peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are increasingly used. This single-centre retrospective study compared indwelling time, clinical utility, and complication profiles between PICCs and CVCs in MICU patients. METHODS: We analyzed 276 MICU patients with either a PICC or CVC, comparing catheter selection, length of stay, dwell time, and complication rates. Complication rates were also standardized per 1000 catheter-days. RESULTS: P P P P P P P P P P P P PICCs were used more frequently in patients with malignancy (< 0.001) or requiring chemotherapy (< 0.001), whereas CVCs were preferred in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (= 0.012), diabetes (= 0.012), COVID-19 (= 0.020), or vasopressor infusion (= 0.001). PICCs were associated with longer indwelling times (≥12 days,< 0.001). In the unstandardized analysis, PICCs had higher rates of catheter dislodgement (< 0.001) and occlusion (= 0.005), but lower rates of puncture-site complications (bleeding, hypersensitivity, fluid leakage; all< 0.05) and deep vein thrombosis incidence (= 0.038). After standardization per 1,000 catheter-days, dislodgement remained significantly more frequent with PICCs, whereas the difference in occlusion was no longer statistically significant. No bloodstream infections occurred with PICCs, versus 5.4% with CVCs (= 0.169). Because groups differed substantially in patient selection, clinical indication, dwell time, insertion site, and securement method, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of superiority. CONCLUSION: PICCs were associated with longer indwelling times and a higher rate of dislodgement, but lower rates of puncture-site complications and deep vein thrombosis; the difference in occlusion was no longer significant after standardization. Vascular access selection should be individualized according to patient characteristics, therapy requirements, anticipated duration, and device-related risks.

title: Development of a machine learning model to predict venous thromboembolism risk in women using combined oral contraceptives.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, with combined oral contraceptives (COCPs) being a modifiable risk factor. Existing clinical tools have limited ability to capture complex predictor interactions. This study aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning (ML) models to predict VTE risk among COCP users. METHODS: This study was conducted using data from the Saudi Real-World Evidence Network (2016–2023). The primary outcome was the first VTE event within 2 years of COCP initiation. Following data partitioning, feature selection was performed on the training set. Elastic-net logistic regression, random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), one-class support vector machine and Isolation-Forest were trained on original and resampled datasets. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and F1 score. RESULTS: The cohort included 24 518 treatment episodes (n=17 512, VTE events=52). After handling class imbalance, RF and XGBoost were the best-performing models (F1: 84.3% and 81.6%; AUROC: 59.6% and 69.2%, respectively), compared with other models (F1: 2.6%–55.3%, AUROC: 54.2%–68.4%). Key predictors included age, glucocorticoid use and rheumatic, renal and thyroid diseases. DISCUSSION: ML shows potential for VTE risk detection despite low event rate and class imbalance. However, findings suggest synthetic sample overfitting, and external validation is warranted before clinical deployment. Identified predictors reinforce the role of metabolic and inflammatory factors in VTE susceptibility among COCP users. CONCLUSION: ML models, particularly XGBoost and RF, demonstrated moderate predictive ability for VTE among COCP users, supporting their use in individualised risk assessments, though external validation is warranted.

title: Association of circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography with preoperative rupture in type A aortic dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography (CTA) and preoperative rupture in patients with type A aortic dissection (TAAD). METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 597 consecutive patients diagnosed with TAAD at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Patients were classified into circumferential dissection (n = 130) and non-circumferential dissection (n = 467) groups based on preoperative CTA. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging characteristics were compared between groups. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to examine factors independently associated with preoperative rupture, and between-group differences in preoperative rupture were compared. RESULTS: Circumferential dissection was strongly associated with DeBakey type I dissection, supra-aortic branch involvement, and greater false-lumen expansion with true-lumen compression. Preoperative rupture occurred more frequently in patients with circumferential dissection than in those without (33.8% vs 7.1%, P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that circumferential dissection was independently associated with preoperative rupture ascertained by bedside echocardiography following the admission CTA after adjustment for demographic, laboratory, and imaging factors (OR = 5.24, 95% CI: 1.86-14.76, P = 0.002). CONCLUSION: Circumferential dissection on CTA is independently associated with preoperative rupture and may support timely surgical decision-making in TAAD.

title: Machine learning models for predicting futile recanalisation after endovascular treatment in patients with large core infarction.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Predicting futile recanalisation following endovascular treatment (EVT) in patients with large core infarctions is crucial for guiding clinical decisions, optimising perioperative management and improving healthcare resource allocation. This study aimed to compare four machine learning (ML) algorithms and identify the most effective model for preinterventional prediction of futile recanalisation. METHODS: Patients achieving successful reperfusion (expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction Score≥2b) from the EVT in Acute Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusive Patients With a Large Infarct Core trial were stratified into two groups: no-futile recanalisation (90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0–3) and futile recanalisation (mRS 4–6). The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression method was used for feature selection, and four ML algorithms, including logistic regression, support vector machine (SVM), decision tree and random forest, were applied. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots and decision curve analysis. Feature importance was ranked using SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) values. RESULTS: Among 146 patients, 74 experienced futile recanalisation. Eight predictors were identified and ranked by SHAP analysis from highest to lowest importance: sex, age, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale, glucose, systolic blood pressure, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, fibrinogen and occlusion site. Among the four models, the SVM model achieved the highest area under the curve of 0.891 (95% CI 0.837 to 0.945), along with good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, p=0.103) and clinical utility. CONCLUSION: The SVM model emerges as the optimal predictive tool for futile recanalisation following EVT in patients with large core infarction. Nevertheless, external validation is required to confirm its performance before clinical application. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04551664.

title: Factors associated with infarct volume growth after mechanical thrombectomy in large core infarction: ANGEL-ASPECT insights.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Infarct volume growth (IVG) correlates with outcomes and may represent a prognostic imaging biomarker in acute ischaemic stroke due to anterior circulation large vessel occlusion (LVO). This study aims to identify factors associated with IVG after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in patients with large core infarction. METHODS: This is a post hoc analysis of the Endovascular Therapy in Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion with a Large Infarct randomised trial. IVG was calculated as final infarct volume minus baseline infarct volume (BIV). The optimal IVG threshold for predicting 90-day favourable outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score 0–3) was determined using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, maximising both sensitivity and specificity. Factors associated with IVG were identified using multivariate logistic regression analyses. RESULTS: Among 228 included patients, ROC analysis identified an optimal IVG threshold of 105 mL for predicting favourable 90-day outcomes (area under the curve=0.71; specificity=0.85, sensitivity=0.53). Patients were stratified into mild (IVG <105 mL, n=150) and severe (IVG ≥105 mL, n=78) groups. Multivariate logistic regression identified BIV (OR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.03; p<0.01), admission blood glucose (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.37; p=0.01), time from puncture to recanalisation (OR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.02; p=0.049) and recanalisation at 36 hours (±12 hours) (OR 0.19, 95% CI 0.05 to 0.72; p=0.01) as independent factors associated with IVG. CONCLUSION: IVG after MT significantly correlates with clinical outcomes. Identification of modifiable IVG determinants after MT may inform periprocedural management strategies in patients with large infarct due to LVO. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04551664.

This study aims to identify factors associated with IVG after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in patients with large core infarction. METHODS: This is a post hoc analysis of the Endovascular Therapy in Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion with a Large Infarct randomised trial.

title: Personalised approach to venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in heavier critically ill patients (PROSPER): A randomised, parallel-group, electronic medical record (EMR)-embedded feasibility trial.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Data are limited regarding optimal low molecular weight heparin dosing for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in heavier critically ill patients. This trial evaluated the feasibility of a weight-based dynamic dosing algorithm. DESIGN SETTING PARTICIPANTS: Open-label, electronic medical record-embedded randomised feasibility trial. Patients, weighing ≥100 kg who required thromboprophylaxis were eligible. Enoxaparin was commenced with weight-based dosing and anti-Xa level-guided adjustment (target peak anti-Xa level 0.2-0.4 IU/mL) or usual care (40 mg twice daily). MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was peak anti-Xa level at 'steady state' (after ≥3 enoxaparin doses). The feasibility threshold was set at 95% of steady state anti-Xa levels in the intervention group being less than the threshold for therapeutic anticoagulant effect (≤0.6 IU/mL). RESULTS: Fifty participants (intervention n = 17, control n = 33) received 331 doses of enoxaparin (median of 4 [interquartile range {IQR}: 3-7] doses per participant, and a dose of 50 [IQR: 50-60] mg (intervention) and 40 [IQR: 40-40] mg (control)). Thirty-two 'steady state' peak anti-Xa measurements were recorded from 24 patients (12 intervention and 12 control). The proportion of peak anti-Xa levels that were ≤0.6 IU/mL was: 15 of 17 (88%) vs. 15 of 15 (100%). There were fewer peak anti-Xa measurements below the prophylactic range (<0.2 IU/mL) in the intervention group compared with the control group (2 of 17 [12%] vs. 5 of 15 [33%]). Six patients developed venous thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (2 of 17 [12%] vs. 4 of 33 [12%]). Major bleeding occurred in one patient in the intervention group. CONCLUSIONS: A weight-based dynamic thromboprophylaxis algorithm was implemented via the electronic medical record but did not meet the predefined feasibility threshold.

title: Tumor necrosis factor inhibitors and cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis is associated with persistent systemic inflammation and increased cardiovascular risk. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. METHODS: The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251270784). Randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies evaluating anti-TNF therapy versus placebo, no anti-TNF exposure, topical therapy and/or phototherapy, or non-biologic systemic therapy were eligible. Outcomes of interest were Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE), myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included. In randomized evidence, anti-TNF therapy was not associated with significant differences in the risk of MACE, myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. In observational analyses stratified by comparator, anti-TNF therapy was associated with a lower pooled risk of reported cardiovascular events versus topical therapy, but not versus oral therapy or phototherapy. STUDY LIMITATIONS: The available evidence was limited by short follow-up in randomized trials, low cardiovascular event counts, wide confidence intervals, and indirect assessment of cardiovascular outcomes, as most trials were designed primarily for dermatologic efficacy and general safety rather than cardiovascular endpoints. CONCLUSIONS: Anti-TNF agents were not associated with a clear increase in major cardiovascular risk and appear to have an acceptable short-term cardiovascular safety profile. However, current evidence does not establish a conclusive cardioprotective effect, and larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed.

title: Efficacy and safety of topical versus intravenous tranexamic acid in primary total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) often leads to substantial perioperative blood loss and postoperative hemoglobin decline, frequently requiring allogeneic transfusions. Tranexamic acid (TXA) effectively reduces bleeding, but debate persists regarding whether topical or intravenous (IV) administration provides superior clinical outcomes.This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of topical versus IV TXA in primary TKA using pooled data from randomized controlled trials (RCTs). METHODS: PubMed was searched for parallel-group RCTs comparing topical and IV TXA. Random-effects models analyzed continuous outcomes via standardized mean differences (SMDs) and dichotomous outcomes via relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Eleven RCTs were included. Pooled analysis demonstrated no statistically significant differences between topical and IV TXA across all metrics. Postoperative hemoglobin drop (9 studies, 815 patients; SMD = -0.292, 95% CI: -0.748 to 0.163, P = 0.208), total blood loss (5 studies, 418 patients; SMD = 0.356, 95% CI: -0.297 to 1.009, P = 0.284), drainage volume (5 studies, 357 patients; SMD = 0.721, 95% CI: -0.394 to 1.836, P = 0.204), and transfusion rate (10 studies, 914 patients; RR = 0.644, 95% CI: 0.343 to 1.209, P = 0.171). Safety data were limited, as usable deep vein thrombosis (DVT) data were reported in only seven studies (with four studies not reporting or not stating thromboembolic/adverse event), and only a single DVT event was reported in the IV group. CONCLUSIONS: In primary TKA, no clear difference was detected between topical and IV TXA for blood conservation, drainage volumes, and transfusion rates, with substantial uncertainty, especially for safety and thromboembolic outcomes.

title: Cause-specific mortality after endovascular treatment for anterior vs. posterior circulation large vessel occlusion: a multicenter cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (AIS-LVO) carries substantial mortality despite endovascular treatment (EVT). Whether causes of death differ between anterior (AVO) and posterior (PVO) circulation occlusions is poorly characterized. We compared cause-specific 90-day mortality between patients with AVO and PVO treated with EVT. METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective cohort, consecutive patients with AIS-LVO who underwent EVT at 111 hospitals in China (ANGEL-ACT registry [Endovascular Treatment Key Technique and Emergency Workflow Improvement of acute ischemic stroke]) were included, and adjudicated causes of death were grouped into prespecified categories. Cause-specific mortality was assessed in the complete analytic cohort using the Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard model, with survivors censored at 90 days and deaths from other causes treated as competing events. Cumulative incidence functions were estimated with the Aalen-Johansen estimator. RESULTS: p p p p p p Among 1,671 eligible patients (1,300 AVO, 371 PVO), 228 deaths (13.6%) occurred within 90 days. All-cause mortality was higher in PVO than AVO (19.4% vs. 12.0%). Cerebral edema-related death was significantly more frequent in PVO than AVO (90-day cumulative incidence 9.16% vs. 4.15%; adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 0.47, 95% CI 0.30-0.73,= 0.001; Gray's test< 0.001). Fatal hemorrhagic transformation was numerically more frequent in AVO but did not reach statistical significance in the complete cohort (3.77% vs. 1.89%; adjusted sHR 1.76, 95% CI 0.78-3.98,= 0.17; Gray's test= 0.076), consistent across all sensitivity analyses. Pneumonia-related (adjusted sHR 0.34, 95% CI 0.17-0.68,= 0.003) and recurrent stroke-related (adjusted sHR 0.29, 95% CI 0.10-0.86,= 0.026) deaths were also more frequent in PVO; the pneumonia association remained significant after Bonferroni correction, whereas the recurrent stroke association did not. CONCLUSION: Fatal complications after EVT differ by occlusion territory. Posterior circulation occlusion is independently associated with a higher risk of death from cerebral edema, pneumonia, and recurrent stroke, although the recurrent stroke association did not survive Bonferroni correction. Hemorrhagic transformation accounted for a larger share of anterior circulation deaths, but this did not correspond to a statistically significant increase in risk in the complete cohort.

Whether causes of death differ between anterior (AVO) and posterior (PVO) circulation occlusions is poorly characterized. We compared cause-specific 90-day mortality between patients with AVO and PVO treated with EVT.

title: Variation and temporal trends in Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group billing for carotid endarterectomy across Vascular Quality Initiative centers.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hospitals use Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) coding to bill for each admission, with higher payment provided for those with complications or comorbidities (CCs) or major CCs (MCCs). We analyzed variation in MS-DRG coding for carotid endarterectomy (CEA) across Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) centers to identify opportunities for improvement. METHODS: We matched CEA cases in the VQI registry with Medicare claims data from 2013 through 2023. A multivariable stepwise logistic regression model was created to identify variables associated with CC or MCC billing (with odds ratios [ORs]). We examined variations in CC or MCC billing percentages among centers and applied a multivariable model to compare observed-to-expected (O:E) CC or MCC billing rates to adjust for patient differences. Billing trends over time were analyzed using linear regression. RESULTS: Among 75,064 primary CEA admissions for Medicare beneficiaries, 39.5% were billed with CCs or MCCs (31.1% CCs, 8.4% MCCs) and 60.5% without. Eleven VQI clinical variables that indicated CCs were significantly associated with CC or MCC billing: dialysis dependence (OR, 22.30), postoperative neurological events (OR, 5.25), length of stay >2 days (OR, 4.98), pre-existing heart failure (OR, 4.08), any postoperative complication (OR, 3.70), reoperation (OR, 3.65), preoperative neurological event (OR, 1.70), higher American Society of Anesthesiologists class (OR, 1.50), urgent/emergent procedure (OR, 1.28), postoperative intravenous blood pressure management (OR, 1.27), and institutional transfer (OR, 1.16). Across 371 VQI centers, CC or MCC billing rates varied 5.6-fold, ranging from 15% to 84% of admissions. After risk adjustment, observed-to-expected ratios still demonstrated 4.2-fold variation, from 0.45 to 1.90 across centers. The observed rate of CC or MCC billing increased over time, from 35.5% in 2015 to 46.1% in 2023 (P < .001). In contrast, the expected adjusted rates predicted by the model remained stable (P = .269). A discrete inflection point was identified between 2016 and 2017, after which higher billing rates persisted (P < .001). CONCLUSIONS: Substantial variation exists for MS-DRG billing for CEA across VQI centers. Billing rates for CCs or MCCs increased from 2013 through 2023. These findings suggest potential underbilling at some centers and overbilling at others. Leveraging Medicare-linked VQI registry data and the proposed model could help to improve coding and billing accuracy, optimize reimbursement, and reduce Medicare audit risk.

title: Predictors of in-hospital venous thromboembolism in patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty.
abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluated the national inpatient incidence, patient characteristics, and independent predictors of VTE following primary THA. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2022. Adult patients undergoing primary THA were identified using ICD-10 procedure codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital VTE, defined as deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism during the index admission. Survey-weighted analyses were used to generate national estimates, compare baseline characteristics, and identify independent predictors of VTE using multivariable logistic regression. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. RESULTS: Among 855,645 weighted inpatient primary THA admissions, 1660 patients developed in-hospital VTE, corresponding to an incidence of 0.19%. Patients with VTE were older (P < 0.001) and more frequently covered by Medicare (P < 0.001), treated at large hospitals (P = 0.009), and treated at urban teaching hospitals (P = 0.013). They also had a greater prevalence of comorbidities, including autoimmune disease, coagulopathy, congestive heart failure, deficiency anemia, peripheral vascular disease, pulmonary circulation disorders, and moderate renal failure (all P < 0.001), as well as chronic pulmonary disease (P = 0.001) and obesity (P = 0.003). On adjusted analysis, the strongest predictors of VTE were paralysis (OR 9.79, P < 0.001), lymphoma (OR 4.35, P = 0.001), other neurologic disorders (OR 4.30, P < 0.001), and pulmonary circulation disorders (OR 3.50, P < 0.001). Additional independent predictors included peripheral vascular disease (OR 2.19, P < 0.001), autoimmune disease (OR 2.01, P < 0.001), congestive heart failure (OR 1.83, P = 0.022), coagulopathy (OR 1.80, P = 0.035), deficiency anemia (OR 1.65, P = 0.002), hypothyroidism (OR 1.45, P = 0.007), and obesity (OR 1.35, P = 0.018). CONCLUSION: In-hospital VTE following primary THA was uncommon but concentrated among medically complex patients. Improved risk stratification may guide perioperative counseling, surveillance, and individualized thromboprophylaxis for higher-risk patients.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2022. Adult patients undergoing primary THA were identified using ICD-10 procedure codes.

title: Patient-specific finite element modeling of image-derived shell morphoelastic growth: A general framework and application to stented aortic dissection.
abstract: Vascular pathology often manifests in complex shape evolution visualized by longitudinal computed tomography (CT) imaging. Growth and remodeling (G&R) frameworks have been integrated into finite element (FE) modeling to probe the mechanics underlying this progression, extending into patient-specific approaches. Their scalability and translatability, however, are limited by the computational burden associated with heterogeneous, anisotropic growth fields and through-thickness meshing. While existing shell growth formulations can mitigate this burden, they require nontrivial FE implementation especially in commercial softwares (e.g., Abaqus) and their efficacy in patient-specific geometries under complex loading is unclear. In this work, we present a general computational framework to implement shell morphoelastic growth computed directly from registered patient-specific CT images. This shell implementation is validated against solid 3D formulations, allows thickness tunability, and increases compatibility with CT surfaces. We demonstrate the robustness of this formulation through modeling post-operative growth in a patient-specific aortic dissection under stent-based loading. Results first show that complex stent-based loading can deform the shell dissection flap to reproduce post-operative geometry. The outer aortic wall is then given a growth field calculated from registration of 1-month and 5-year post-operative CT images, which is implemented along with stent-based loading and pressurization. Results from this model capture the trends in total and lumen morphological evolution observed at intermediate timepoints. These findings establish a general framework, validated with a patient-specific case study of aortic dissection, with the potential to expand to other complex systems, scale to larger patient populations, and apply G&R to clinical translation.

title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyzes reveal hepatic regulatory mechanisms of residual feed intake during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers.
abstract: This study aimed to characterize hepatic molecular features associated with residual feed intake (RFI) during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers through integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyzes. RFI was measured in 478 individually caged male Langya chickens from 96 to 133 days of age. After the feeding trial, the chickens were ranked in ascending order of RFI and classified into low-RFI (LRFI) and high-RFI (HRFI) subpopulations using the population mean RFI as the cutoff. Eight healthy chickens were then randomly selected from each subpopulation to form the LRFI and HRFI groups (n = 8 per group). Following slaughter and tissue collection at 133 days of age, hepatic transcriptomic and LC-MS-based untargeted metabolomic analyzes were conducted. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) were subsequently subjected to enrichment and correlation analyzes. Compared with HRFI chickens, LRFI chickens had lower feed intake (FI) and higher eviscerated carcass yield and breast muscle yield. They also had lower abdominal fat percentage and muscle fat width, whereas BWG and metabolic body weight were similar between groups. Liver profiling identified 850 DEGs and 282 DAMs. Integrated KEGG analysis identified 15 pathways significantly enriched in both datasets. The amino acid metabolism-related pathways among these shared pathways collectively pointed to aromatic amino acid (AAA)-related metabolism, including biosynthesis of amino acids, phenylalanine metabolism, phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan biosynthesis, and tryptophan metabolism. A total of 16 DEGs and 29 DAMs were mapped to these pathways and showed widespread significant correlations. Among them, IL4I1, AFMID, ASS1, PHGDH, MAOB, IDO2, HAAO, and PAH were identified as candidate genes associated with RFI. These results characterized hepatic molecular features associated with RFI during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers. These findings indicate that hepatic AAA-related metabolism may play a potential role in RFI divergence during the late growth stage in slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers. The identified AAA metabolism-related pathways provide a focused set of candidate genes, metabolites, and pathways for further investigation of their roles in RFI and feed efficiency, and provide a theoretical basis for molecular breeding and breed conservation of slow-growing broilers.

title: PASCAL Precision System Outcomes by Implant Location and Lesion Location in Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation Patients From the STS/ACC TVT Registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be more challenging in noncentral regions of the valve and in anterior or bileaflet lesions. We assess effect of implant location and leaflet lesion location on safety and effectiveness of PASCAL Precision system in degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR). METHODS: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair outcomes in patients with degenerative MR treated with PASCAL Precision system (September 2022-October 2024), from the US STS/ACC TVT (Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy) Registry, were analyzed by implant location (A2P2/non-A2P2) and leaflet lesion location (anterior/posterior/bileaflet). Procedural, clinical, and echocardiographic outcomes to 30 days were assessed. RESULTS: P P P P P P P P At 30 days, both A2P2 (n=1526) and non-A2P2 (n=299) groups had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 1.1% versus 1.0%, mitral valve reintervention: 0.4% versus 0.0% and single leaflet device attachment: 0.5% versus 0.3%; all>0.05) and demonstrated significant MR reduction (<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference between groups (=0.750) (MR ≤2+: 93.4% versus 95.4%; MR ≤1+: 72.0% versus 73.3%). Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores improved significantly in both groups (∆19.3, ∆17.7 points;=0.741). The anterior (n=250), posterior (n=902), and bileaflet (n=192) disease groups also had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 0.4%, 1.1%, 0.0%; mitral valve reintervention: 0.8%, 0.1%, 0.5%; and single leaflet device attachment: 0.8%, 0.2%, 0.5%; all>0.05), and demonstrated significant MR reduction (<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference across groups (=0.459) (MR ≤2+: 94.1%, 93.1%, and 94.5%; MR ≤1+: 79.0%, 69.2%, and 72.4%). All groups experienced significant improvement in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores (∆21.4, ∆18.8, ∆12.0 points;=0.087). CONCLUSION: In real-world patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation, treatment with the PASCAL Precision system was associated with favorable safety and effectiveness at 30 days, regardless of implant location or leaflet lesion location.

title: Surgical management of splenic artery aneurysms: a case series of three patients with diverse presentations.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Splenic artery aneurysm (SAA) is the most common visceral artery aneurysm and includes true aneurysms and pseudoaneurysms, which have different etiologies and clinical behavior. Presentation ranges from incidental detection to life-threatening rupture with hemoperitoneum. Management depends on aneurysm size, symptoms, morphology, anatomical relationships, comorbidities, and rupture status. METHODS: We retrospectively described three consecutive patients with SAA or pseudoaneurysm treated surgically at a tertiary surgical center, Loghman Hakim Hospital, Shahid Beheshti University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran, between 2020 and 2025. Clinical records, imaging, operative findings, histopathology, postoperative course, and available follow-up were reviewed. The series was reported in accordance with the PROCESS 2025 reporting guideline. CASE PRESENTATIONS: Case 1 was a 66-year-old man with chronic liver disease and thrombocytopenia in whom a giant true SAA measuring approximately 72 × 68 × 76 mm was incidentally identified during trauma imaging. The aneurysm was adjacent to the pancreatic body without rupture. Elective open splenectomy with aneurysm resection and concurrent liver wedge biopsy was performed. Case 2 was a 63-year-old woman with a 7-month history of postprandial epigastric pain and a symptomatic true SAA of undocumented size. Elective open resection with splenectomy was performed; histopathology unexpectedly demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous splenitis. Case 3 was a 38-year-old woman with sickle cell disease who developed acute abdominal pain after a generalized seizure, with severe anemia and hemoperitoneum. A ruptured splenic artery pseudoaneurysm was identified at emergency laparotomy after a ruptured ectopic pregnancy had initially been suspected. RESULTS: All three patients underwent open splenectomy with aneurysm excision, which was elective in cases 1 and 2 and emergent in case 3. There were no intraoperative deaths or reoperations. All three patients had uneventful postoperative recoveries. 6-month follow-up was available for case 1; longer-term uniform follow-up was not available for all patients. CONCLUSION: SAAs encompass a broad clinical spectrum, from incidentally discovered giant aneurysms to symptomatic lesions and catastrophic rupture. These cases illustrate the importance of anatomy-directed treatment selection, early recognition of rupture, and consideration of vascular causes in patients with unexplained hemoperitoneum. Endovascular therapy is preferred for anatomically suitable elective lesions, whereas open surgery remains an important option for giant, complex, or ruptured aneurysms. The proposed algorithm is an educational synthesis of published evidence, current Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines recommendations, and the clinical experience represented by this institutional series rather than a prospectively validated decision tool.

title: Early antithrombotic therapy improves 90-day functional outcomes in patients with postinterventional cerebral hyperdensity after mechanical thrombectomy: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Postinterventional cerebral hyperdensity (PCHD) is a specific type of hyperdensity commonly observed on computed tomography (CT) scans of the head after mechanical thrombectomy (MT). This study aimed to investigate the association between early antithrombotic therapy (EAT) and 90-day functional outcomes in anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke (acAIS) patients with PCHD. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 141 consecutive acAIS patients with PCHD after MT. EAT was defined as antithrombotic therapy administered within 24 h post-MT. The primary outcome was a favorable 90-day functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2). The secondary outcomes included 90-day mortality, ΔmRS (defined as the mRS score before MT minus the 90-day mRS score), enlargement of cerebral hyperdensity, and persistent hyperdensity on the 24-h follow-up CT graded by the European Cooperative Acute Stroke Study (ECASS III) morphology. Baseline and outcome data were compared between the EAT and non-EAT groups. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the association between EAT and favorable outcomes. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the robustness and internal consistency of the results. RESULTS: p p p p Of the 129 patients with complete 90-day mRS data, 59 (45.7%) received EAT. The EAT group had a higher proportion of favorable outcomes (59.3% vs. 37.1%,= 0.019). A multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that EAT remained significantly associated with favorable outcomes (Model 1: odds ratio (OR) 2.469, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.195-5.104,= 0.015; Model 2: OR 2.72, 95% CI 1.02-7.20,= 0.045; Model 3: OR 3.68, 95% CI 1.32-10.30,= 0.013), and the results were consistent after imputation based on discharge data and multiple imputation. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses showed consistent results, with no significant interaction effects observed. CONCLUSION: EAT is associated with improved 90-day functional outcomes in acAIS patients with PCHD, warranting further investigation in larger prospective studies.
