title: Association of the triglyceride-glucose index with the severity of lower extremity arterial disease across glucose metabolic states: a single-center cross-sectional study of 656 patients with angiographically confirmed disease.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To examine the cross-sectional association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and the severity of lower extremity arterial disease (LEAD) in hospitalized patients with angiographically confirmed LEAD, to test whether this association differs across Glucose Metabolic States, and to quantify the ability of the TyG index to discriminate prevalent ischemic tissue loss (Rutherford grades 5-6). METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study included 656 consecutive patients with angiographically confirmed LEAD who were hospitalized in the Department of Vascular Surgery at the General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University from January 2023 through December 2024. Diagnosis was confirmed by digital subtraction angiography (DSA). Patients were classified into four groups according to their Glucose Metabolic States: normal glucose tolerance (NGT, n = 150), impaired glucose regulation (IGR, n = 148), diabetes with a duration of <10 years (DM<10y, n = 174), and diabetes with a duration of ≥10 years (DM≥10y, n = 184). Glucose and lipid parameters and LEAD severity (Rutherford classification) were assessed during the same hospitalization. Spearman correlation, multinomial logistic regression (with grade 1 mild claudication as the reference), ordinal logistic regression with a TyG × Glucose Metabolic States interaction term, proportional-odds assessment by cumulative binary splits, ROC analysis with bootstrap internal validation (1,000 resamples), and decision-curve analysis were performed. Sensitivity analyses used continuous glycemic measures instead of the categorical groups, excluded implausibly low fasting glucose values, and added liver enzymes to the adjustment set. The primary outcome was ischemic tissue loss, defined as Rutherford grades 5-6 (n = 205, 31.2%). RESULTS: The TyG index increased progressively across Glucose Metabolic States categories (8.79 ± 0.51, 9.15 ± 0.48, 9.57 ± 0.56, and 9.67 ± 0.52 for NGT, IGR, DM < 10 years, and DM ≥ 10 years, respectively; P < 0.001) and was strongly correlated with Rutherford grade (Spearman r = 0.677, P < 0.001). In a multinomial logistic regression model adjusted for age, sex, smoking, hypertension, BMI, and fatty liver disease (all variance inflation factors < 1.5), the TyG index remained associated with each severity category above the reference, with adjusted odds ratios per 0.5-unit increment of 2.51 (grade 2), 2.83 (grade 3), 7.56 (grade 4), 9.62 (grade 5), and 20.45 (grade 6). The interaction between TyG and Glucose Metabolic States was statistically significant (likelihood-ratio χ² = 95.63, df = 3, P < 0.001); stratum-specific odds ratios per 0.5-unit increment were 1.51 (95% CI 1.07-2.13) in IGR, 2.50 (1.90-3.29) in DM < 10 years, and 8.14 (5.23-12.67) in DM ≥ 10 years, whereas the NGT-stratum estimate was unstable (quasi-complete separation) and could not be interpreted. When the categorical groups were replaced with a continuous glycemic measure, the interaction with fasting plasma glucose remained significant but was in the opposite direction (χ² = 9.36, df = 1, P = 0.002): the TyG-severity association was stronger at lower fasting glucose levels (OR per 0.5 unit 4.81 at 4.8 mmol/L) than at higher fasting glucose levels (3.46 at 8.3 mmol/L). For discriminating Rutherford grades 5-6, the AUC was 0.833 (95% CI 0.796-0.870); the Youden-optimal cutoff was 9.42 (sensitivity 85.9%, specificity 71.0%, positive predictive value 57.3%, negative predictive value 91.7%, LR + 2.96, LR- 0.199), and this cutoff was stable across bootstrap resamples. Decision-curve analysis showed a positive net benefit relative to treat-all or treat-none strategies across threshold probabilities of approximately 0.09-0.57. CONCLUSION: In this cohort of patients with angiographically confirmed LEAD, the TyG index was independently associated with LEAD severity. The strength of this association appeared to vary across Glucose Metabolic States, but the apparent gradient from normal glucose tolerance to long-standing diabetes was not reproduced when glucose was modelled continuously, suggesting that part of the categorical pattern is attributable to the grouping itself (i.e., mathematical coupling and range restriction). The TyG index showed moderate ability to discriminate prevalent ischemic tissue loss. Because exposure and outcome were assessed during the same hospitalization, these findings represent a cross-sectional association rather than a predictive one; the proposed cutoff values were derived from the same sample in which they were evaluated and require external validation before they can be considered for clinical use.

METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study included 656 consecutive patients with angiographically confirmed LEAD who were hospitalized in the Department of Vascular Surgery at the General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University from January 2023 through December 2024. Diagnosis was confirmed by digital subtraction angiography (DSA).

title: Added value of brain perfusion ultrasound to prehospital stroke scales-a secondary analysis of the SONAS trial.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Accurate prehospital identification of acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (LVO) is critical to guide selection of an optimal target hospital for either intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) alone and/or mechanical thrombectomy (MT). The novel portable non-imaging brain perfusion ultrasound (BPU) device SONAS(TM) indicated similar sensitivity and specificity as prehospital stroke scales. In this study, we reanalyzed data from the original 20 patient cohort to evaluate whether combining BPU with prehospital stroke scales (ph-SS) can further improve LVO detection. METHODS: Clinical data and NIHSS scores of all patients suffering from acute ischemic stroke with and without proven LVO in the SONAS trial were collected and applied to 16 different phSS. As an exploratory analysis we also applied a prehospital score for intracerebral hemorrhage (ph-ICH) to this cohort. The positive and negative predictive values as well as sensitivity and specificity were analyzed retrospectively for both methods. RESULTS: The best performing phSS, CG-FAST, and RACE, showed comparable performances to BPU, but still misdiagnosed patients. However, in our specific cohort, the combination of both methods allowed for a reliable classification into three groups: (A) "highly probably LVO", (B) "highly probable non-LVO" and (C) "not assessable" (including all patients misdiagnosed by one method alone). The addition of BPU resulted in shifts towards higher sensitivity and NPV. When using the ph-ICH score three patients were classified as ICH (false positive), and all of them showed severe perfusion deficits in BPU indicating LVO. CONCLUSION: The combination of BPU with phSS may hold the potential to enhance prehospital triage of acute stroke patients selecting patients to (A) endovascular-capable centers, (B) the nearest stroke unit for, i.e., IVT or (C) either depending on other clinical factors and local circumstances. However, validation is critical in stroke-call patients in the prehospital setting including application by paramedics with/without emergency physicians or telemedical support, and compared to other prehospital point-of-care diagnostics both in respect to sensitivity/specificity, timeline and, ultimately, costs. In the future, the addition of serum biomarkers for ICH may open new opportunities for early ICH treatment or even enable prehospital IVT, and/or streamline direct to angio-suite approaches in confirmed LVO.

In this study, we reanalyzed data from the original 20 patient cohort to evaluate whether combining BPU with prehospital stroke scales (ph-SS) can further improve LVO detection.

title: Factors associated with failures and outcomes of Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: to analyze factors associated with catheter progression failure and outcomes of Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters inserted by nurses in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. METHOD: observational cohort study was conducted with hospitalized COVID-19 patients, following the STROBE guidelines. Categorical variables were described as absolute and relative frequencies; quantitative variables were expressed as median and interquartile range. Non-parametric tests were applied due to non-normal distribution. Associations were analyzed using Pearson's chi-squared or Fisher's exact tests. Logistic regression was performed for variables associated with outcomes. RESULTS: a total of 1061 Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters were analyzed. The main indications were for antibiotic therapy, and most catheters were removed after treatment completion. First-attempt failure and clinical patient profile were associated with catheter progression failure. Subcutaneous heparin was a protective factor. Among Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters successfully inserted, tip confirmation via chest X-ray and catheter-to-vessel ratio between 31%-40% were associated with thrombosis, whereas Sherlock™ confirmation was protective. CONCLUSION: catheter progression failure was associated with clinical conditions and first-attempt failure. Adverse outcomes were associated with X-ray tip confirmation and catheter-to-vessel ratio, whereas Sherlock™ use and subcutaneous heparin were protective factors.

title: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Endovascular and Open Surgical Repair for Infective Native Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Infective native aortic aneurysms (mycotic) are rare but highly lethal, and the optimal treatment strategy between endovascular repair and open surgical repair (OSR) remains debated because of a persistent trade-off between early survival and durable infection control. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing early and long-term outcomes of endovascular repair and OSR, complemented by a single-arm meta-analysis characterizing outcomes after endovascular repair. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 16, 2026. Comparative studies were pooled using inverse-variance random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation of between-study variance (odds ratios [ORs]); single-arm proportions were pooled using logit-transformed, inverse-variance-weighted random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed with Risk of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions-I. Outcomes included 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality, reinfection (a new or persistent infection requiring antimicrobial therapy or source control), sepsis recurrence (a new episode meeting sepsis criteria after initial clinical resolution), reintervention, and acute kidney injury (AKI). RESULTS: Thirty-five retrospective studies were included: 18 comparative studies (2,853 enrolled patients; 1,305 endovascular repair and 1,548 OSR; 17 of which, comprising 2,836 patients, reported 30-day mortality) and 17 single-arm studies (444 endovascular repair patients; 16 of which reported 30-day mortality). Endovascular repair was associated with significantly lower 30-day mortality than OSR (OR 0.72, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.55-0.93) but not with 1-year mortality (eight studies, 1,630 patients; OR 1.23, 95% CI 0.66-2.29), and with a higher risk of reinfection (14 studies, 1,448 patients; OR 2.56, 95% CI 1.71-3.82). No significant differences were found for sepsis recurrence, reintervention, or AKI, though these comparisons were imprecise and compatible with both clinically meaningful benefit and harm, and should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence between strategies. In the single-arm analysis, pooled 30-day mortality after endovascular repair was 6.5%, 1-year mortality was 22.4%, and reinfection was 14.7%. CONCLUSION: In pooled analysis, endovascular repair was associated with lower early mortality compared with open surgical repair, although this finding was sensitive to the inclusion of a single large registry-based study and should be interpreted with caution. No significant difference in 1-year mortality was observed, but this comparison was imprecise and based on few studies and should not be interpreted as evidence that a survival advantage is absent. Endovascular repair carries a higher risk of reinfection. Careful patient selection, prolonged antimicrobial therapy, and structured postoperative surveillance remain essential regardless of the repair strategy chosen. Certainty of evidence for all comparative outcomes was very low (GRADE), reflecting the observational design, serious risk of confounding by indication, and imprecision of the pooled estimates.

title: Lesion Water Content on CT Predicts 12-Month Outcome and Modifies Thrombectomy Effect in Large-Core Stroke-A Secondary Analysis of the TENSION Trial.
abstract: In large-core ischemic stroke, outcomes after thrombectomy remain heterogeneous, and imaging markers that capture treatment-modifiable injury beyond lesion extent are needed. We investigated whether lesion water content on noncontrast CT, quantified as net water uptake (NWU), predicts 12-month functional outcome and modifies the effect of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). This secondary analysis of the randomized TENSION trial included 198 patients with admission CT suitable for NWU quantification and available 12-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores; 168 had paired 24-h CT for follow-up NWU (NWUFU) assessment. The primary outcome was ordinal 12-month mRS. Multivariable ordinal and logistic regression tested associations and the NWU × EVT interaction, with discrimination assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Median baseline NWU was 16.4% and NWUFU 28.9%. At 12 months, 45 patients (23%) had mRS 0-3 and 111 (56%) had died. Higher baseline NWU independently predicted worse 12-month mRS (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR], 1.10 per percentage-point; 95% CI, 1.05-1.16; P < 0.001) and modified the EVT effect (interaction acOR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.06-1.30; P = 0.002), with greater discrimination than ASPECTS. NWUFU was the strongest single imaging predictor (acOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.06-1.14; P < 0.001; AUC, 0.78 for mRS 0-3) and superseded baseline NWU when co-modeled. Among 97 90-day survivors, higher NWUFU independently predicted late mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02-1.18; P = 0.019). Lesion water content may therefore provide a clinically accessible CT biomarker linking treatment-modifiable injury at baseline with realized post-treatment injury and long-term outcome.

title: Contact Aspiration Versus Combined Thrombectomy in Basilar Artery Occlusion: Clinical Severity and First-pass Recanalization Are Associated with Outcome.
abstract: PURPOSE: Acute basilar artery occlusion (BAO) carries high rates of death and disability despite endovascular therapy, and the optimal technique remains unclear. We compared contact aspiration (CA) alone with combined CA plus stent retriever (CA + SR) and identified factors associated with first-pass reperfusion and 3‑month outcome. METHODS: In the prospective multicenter SARA-3 registry, the primary outcomes compared between CA and CA + SR were first-pass recanalization (modified Treatment in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 2b-3) and 3‑month functional independence. Secondary outcomes were final recanalization, procedural time, safety, 24‑h NIHSS, and mortality. Factors associated with unfavorable outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 3-6) were assessed by Firth penalized logistic regression, with first-line technique forced in as a sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Among 68 patients (median admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] 11), 50 (73.5%) received CA and 18 (26.5%) CA + SR. The two techniques showed no statistically significant differences in reperfusion, safety, or 3‑month unfavorable outcome (48% vs. 53%; underpowered), but CA was faster (21 vs. 38 min; P = 0.007). Admission NIHSS (odds ratio [OR] 1.08 per point; P = 0.004) and first-pass mTICI 2b-3 (OR 0.06; P < 0.001) were independently associated with outcome; their combination discriminated well (area under the curve 0.83). Forcing technique into the model did not change these associations (CA + SR adjusted OR 1.19; P = 0.81). No baseline characteristic was independently associated with first-pass reperfusion. CONCLUSIONS: CA and CA + SR showed no statistically significant difference in 3‑month outcomes, but CA was faster. First-line technique was not associated with functional outcome; instead, outcome reflected baseline stroke severity and first-pass reperfusion, which defined prognostic groups that may aid risk stratification if externally validated.

title: AI-enhanced intraoperative decision-making in robotic surgery: from augmented reality navigation to foundation models.
abstract: Robotic surgical platforms have improved instrument dexterity, tremor filtration, and ergonomic control, yet intraoperative decisions still depend on a surgeon interpreting a moving, partially observed field under time pressure. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to close parts of this loop by recognizing anatomy, tracking instruments, anticipating events, and-experimentally-planning or executing selected actions. This review maps the computational technologies that support intraoperative decision-making in robotic surgery and appraises the clinical evidence for them.Because the direct robotic evidence base is still uneven, we explicitly distinguish three kinds of material: (i) studies conducted on robotic systems during surgery; (ii) non-robotic surgical evidence from laparoscopic and thoracoscopic procedures that use the same vision and workflow methods; and (iii) preclinical, preoperative, and perioperative work that is conceptually relevant but not intraoperative. Robotic and non-robotic settings are labeled throughout the tables and text. We further separate non-AI image guidance-indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence and registered overlays-from AI-based inference, and we include image-guided endovascular robotics as a complementary setting in which fluoroscopic perception, vascular-topology reasoning, and closed-loop instrument control are particularly advanced.We organize the field into four computational layers: perception, anatomical and procedural reasoning, action planning, and control and execution. Augmented-reality and fluorescence navigation can improve orientation and selected intermediate outcomes, and several randomized trials now exist. Computer-vision systems can recognize anatomy, phases, instruments, and adverse events, and in endovascular work they can track guidewires and reason over vascular topology. Foundation models broaden language and multimodal capabilities but remain, in surgery, largely preclinical. Autonomous subtasks have shown promise in phantoms, animals, and a small number of carefully bounded tissue tasks; no system has demonstrated safe, accountable patient-level autonomous decision-making.Navigation and AI-assisted systems have improved orientation, reduced ischemia, and accelerated recognition of critical events in some studies. Whether these intermediate gains improve patient outcomes, generalize across institutions, or justify their cost remains unknown. The question is not whether AI can interpret surgical scenes, but which decisions can be delegated, with what evidence, uncertainty limits, oversight, and outcome measures.

title: Anticoagulation management in a pediatric patient with protein S deficiency and acute pulmonary embolism undergoing ECMO-supported intervention: a case report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Protein S deficiency is a predominant form of hereditary thrombophilia in Asian populations. Pediatric venous thromboembolism (VTE) is exceedingly rare, with an incidence of only 0.2%-0.6%, and acute massive pulmonary embolism (PE) requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support in children with thrombophilia presents exceptional clinical challenges. The core therapeutic dilemma lies in reconciling the hypercoagulable state inherent to protein S deficiency with the high bleeding risk following thrombolytic therapy, compounded by the obligatory anticoagulation requirement during ECMO. This case report describes the nursing management of a pediatric patient with protein S deficiency and acute PE who successfully underwent ECMO-supported interventional treatment under high bleeding risk. OUTCOME: The patient was successfully weaned from ECMO after 98 h of support, extubated on day 6, and discharged in stable condition after 30 days of hospitalization. At 6-month follow-up, no thrombus recurrence was observed, and the patient had fully resumed normal life and academic activities. CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates that an individualized low-dose heparin anticoagulation strategy, guided by the PEACE consensus and supported by meticulous monitoring, can effectively balance the competing risks of thrombosis and hemorrhage in pediatric ECMO patients with underlying thrombophilia and recent thrombolysis. Notably, as a single case report, this finding cannot be broadly generalized to all pediatric ECMO patients with thrombophilia. Instead, this case provides a potential framework for individualized anticoagulation and nursing management that requires further validation in larger pediatric cohorts. The nursing experience provides a practical reference for managing similar complex cases in pediatric critical care.

title: Quality and reliability of short videos about type A aortic dissection on Bilibili and TikTok: a cross-sectional study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type A aortic dissection (TAAD) is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Short-video platforms such as TikTok and Bilibili have become important channels for health information dissemination, but the quality and reliability of TAAD-related videos remain unclear. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the quality and reliability of TAAD-related short videos on TikTok and Bilibili, with particular attention to platform differences and uploader characteristics. METHODS: The top 250 videos ranked by comprehensive ranking on each platform were screened using the Chinese keyword "A." A total of 391 eligible videos were included. Uploaders were classified as medical practitioners, individual users, or institutions. Video quality and reliability were assessed using the Global Quality Score (GQS), modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), JAMA benchmarks, and Video Information Quality Instrument (VIQI). Multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with video quality. RESULTS: TikTok videos showed higher engagement, whereas Bilibili videos were longer and provided broader coverage of epidemiology, etiology, and clinical presentation-related content. TikTok remained independently associated with higher VIQI scores after adjustment. Medical practitioners and institutions generally achieved higher VIQI and JAMA scores than individual users, and content coverage score was independently associated with higher video quality. However, mDISCERN scores did not differ significantly among uploader types. CONCLUSION: TAAD-related short videos demonstrated moderate overall quality but limited reliability. Platform characteristics, uploader type, and content coverage were associated with assessed information quality. Professional participation may improve some aspects of health communication, but uploader identity alone does not ensure higher reliability or transparency.

title: Trends, outcomes and patient- and hospital-level factors associated with sepsis following cesarean delivery: a propensity-matched nationwide inpatient analysis (2016-2022).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a major global health concern and a serious complication of cesarean delivery. However, contemporary nationwide data describing both the temporal trend in post-cesarean sepsis and its downstream clinical and economic burden-particularly in propensity-matched comparisons-remain limited. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, propensity-matched analysis of all adult inpatients undergoing cesarean delivery recorded in the U.S. Nationwide Inpatient Sample (NIS, 2016-2022). Sepsis and cesarean delivery were defined using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes. After 1:5 propensity-score matching on demographics, comorbidity burden and hospital characteristics, we compared in-hospital mortality, length of stay (LOS), total hospitalization costs, and the incidence of perioperative complications between septic and non-septic patients. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify patient- and hospital-level factors independently associated with sepsis. RESULTS: n P P P Of 1,619,187 hospitalizations for cesarean delivery, 1,589,186 adults met the inclusion criteria. Annual sepsis prevalence rose from 0.058% in 2016 to 0.136% in 2022. In the 1:5 propensity-matched cohort ( = 10,050), septic patients had markedly higher in-hospital mortality (2.4% vs. 0.0%, < 0.001), longer median LOS (6 vs. 3 days, < 0.001), and approximately 2.6-fold higher median total hospitalization costs (USD 71,466 vs. USD 27,063, < 0.001). Non-elective admission, treatment in teaching hospitals, a higher comorbidity burden, Asian/Pacific Islander race, and hospital region were independently associated with sepsis. After propensity matching, septic patients also showed substantially elevated adjusted odds of pulmonary embolism (OR 61.7), postoperative shock (OR 28.7), deep-vein thrombosis (OR 24.6), urinary tract infection (OR 25.5), and chronic respiratory diseases (OR 13.2). CONCLUSIONS: In this large U.S. study, sepsis after cesarean section was linked to much higher death rates, twice the hospital stay, about 2.6 times higher costs, and more severe problems like blood clots, shock, infections, and heavy bleeding. These results show that post-cesarean section sepsis is a growing concern, remind us to spot at-risk mothers early, and offer a benchmark against which prevention and cost-effective care can be evaluated.

title: Perforated marginal ulcer after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass: a national analysis of operative approaches, outcomes, and practice variations, 2018-2022.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Perforated marginal (gastrojejunal) ulcer is an uncommon but life-threatening complication after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. Evidence is limited to single-center series and one 2022 systematic review of approximately 600 patients; contemporary national International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10)-era data are lacking. METHODS: We queried the National Inpatient Sample (2018-2022) for adults with a perforated gastrojejunal ulcer and a code indicating prior bariatric surgery. Operative approach was classified as laparoscopic patch, open patch, revisional gastrojejunostomy/reversal, or non-operative management. Survey-weighted statistics, negative-binomial (length of stay), gamma (total charges), and logistic (predictors of operative repair) models were estimated with hospital cluster-robust standard errors. RESULTS: The cohort included 1,669 unweighted admissions (8,345 weighted). Operative repair was performed in 28.9% (laparoscopic patch 12.6%, open patch 7.2%, revisional/reversal 9.2%); 71.1% were managed non-operatively. Crude in-hospital mortality was 1.1% overall. Non-operative management rose from 64.1% (2018) to 72.0% (2022), while laparoscopic patch declined from 18.1% to 12.1%. Open patch was associated with longer length of stay than laparoscopic patch [incidence-rate ratio 1.41, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.13-1.77] and higher complication rates after correction for multiple comparisons of sepsis, acute kidney injury, respiratory failure, and venous thromboembolism. Elective admission strongly predicted operative repair (adjusted odds ratio 2.58, 95% CI 1.74-3.83), elective admissions were concentrated in the revisional group, but the reason for elective admission could not be determined from administrative data. Operative rates declined modestly each year (adjusted odds ratio 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-0.98). Case mix differed between laparoscopic-first and open-first centers. CONCLUSIONS: In the largest contemporary national cohort to date, non-operative management dominated and increased during 2018-2022. Among operatively managed patients, laparoscopic patch repair was associated with shorter length of stay and a more favorable complication profile than open repair. Because operative approach was not randomized and patients selected for open repair may have carried greater physiologic severity or technical complexity, these associations support-but do not establish-a laparoscopic-first approach where anatomy and physiology permit. Prospective evidence is needed to refine operative vs. non-operative triage.

Evidence is limited to single-center series and one 2022 systematic review of approximately 600 patients; contemporary national International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10)-era data are lacking. METHODS: We queried the National Inpatient Sample (2018-2022) for adults with a perforated gastrojejunal ulcer and a code indicating prior bariatric surgery.

title: Aortic Dissection Incidentally Detected on PET/CT During Evaluation for Suspected Multiple Myeloma.
abstract: The identification and diagnosis of aortic dissection on PET/CT remain challenging without the use of contrast agents. Such cases are prone to misdiagnosis or being overlooked, particularly when the examination is focused on an unrelated primary clinical objective. We present a case of thoracic aortic dissection that was incidentally detected on initial PET/CT during the further evaluation of suspected multiple myeloma. The FDG-avid lesion was initially mistaken for an esophageal mass, with differential diagnoses including extramedullary plasmacytoma associated with multiple myeloma and primary esophageal neoplasm.

title: Risk factors and clinical outcomes of reocclusion after endovascular treatment for acute ischemic stroke: an updated systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined. METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE. Post hoc sensitivity analyses included only same-site reocclusion definitions. RESULTS: Ten studies (3,381 patients) were included; 244 (7.2%) reoccluded. Reocclusion was associated with lower 90-day functional independence (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.17-0.38) and higher mortality (OR 1.86, 1.29-2.68), both moderate certainty. Reocclusion was more frequent with large-artery atherosclerosis (OR 2.24, 1.41-3.55; same-site 3.04, 1.73-5.33) and less frequent with cardioembolism (OR 0.40, 0.28-0.57) and atrial fibrillation (OR 0.39, 0.26-0.59), mutually confounded associations reflecting one embolic-versus-atherothrombotic axis. Prestroke antiplatelet therapy (OR 0.43, 0.28-0.67) lost significance under the same-site definition (0.60, 0.31-1.16). Exploratory data (two cohorts) linked eTICI 2c-3 reperfusion with less reocclusion (OR 0.44, 0.28-0.69). No study reported when etiology was adjudicated; the atherosclerosis association may be partly outcome-induced. CONCLUSIONS: Early reocclusion is uncommon but carries a substantial prognostic penalty. Its determinants appear to lie in the vascular substrate rather than thrombectomy technique; prospective studies with uniform same-site definitions and systematic follow-up imaging are needed.

METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE.

title: Analysis of risk factors for venous thromboembolism in hospitalized patients with acute herpetic neuralgia and construction of a predictive nomogram model.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To explore the risk factors for venous thromboembolism (VTE) in hospitalized patients with acute herpetic neuralgia (AHN) and to construct a VTE prediction model based on clinical indicators to help clinicians better identify high-risk patients and develop prevention and treatment strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study retrospectively included 327 patients diagnosed with AHN who were hospitalized in the Pain Department of Hengshui People's Hospital between December 2020 and December 2023, of whom 26 developed VTE during hospitalization. The basic clinical data of the patients were collected, and the independent risk factors for VTE were screened by LASSO regression and multifactorial Logistic regression analysis, and the VTE prediction model was constructed. Model performance was evaluated by ROC curves, calibration curves, and decision curves, and internal validation was performed using ten-fold cross-validation and bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: P P P P The incidence of VTE in AHN patients was 7.95%. LASSO regression screened for 10 relevant variables, and final multifactor logistic regression analysis identified FIB (fibrinogen), FDP (fibrin degradation products), NRS (Numerical Rating Scale) score, and thrombotic risk score as independent predictors. Among them, FIB was a protective factor for VTE (OR = 0.477,= 0.006), while FDP (OR = 1.48,< 0.001), NRS score (OR = 1.584,= 0.039), and thrombotic risk score (OR = 2.05,< 0.001) were risk factors. The AUC of the prediction model was 0.853 (95% CI: 0.764-0.941), and the bootstrap optimism-corrected C-index was 0.834. At the optimal cutoff, the sensitivity and specificity were 0.731 and 0.877, respectively, with good calibration and clinical applicability. CONCLUSIONS: In this study, a VTE prediction model was constructed for patients with AHN. The model can accurately predict the risk of VTE in patients with AHN and provide a reference for clinical prevention and intervention; however, external validation in larger, multicenter cohorts is warranted before clinical implementation.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven imaging-based prediction models for hemorrhagic transformation after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Hemorrhagic transformation (HT) is a major complication after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Although artificial intelligence (AI)-driven imaging-based prediction models have shown promise for predicting HT, their overall predictive performance remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated their predictive performance. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and CBM/SinoMed were searched from inception to July 2, 2026. Studies developing or validating AI-driven imaging-based prediction models for predicting HT after MT in AIS, including both pre- and post-procedural imaging predictors, were included. A random-effects model was used to pool the area under the curve (AUC), while a bivariate random-effects model was used to jointly estimate pooled sensitivity and specificity and construct the SROC curve. Subgroup analyses explored potential sources of heterogeneity. RESULTS: N I p 2 Eleven studies (total = 3,541) were included, 10 studies contributed eligible AUC estimates, with evaluation cohorts ranging from 18 to 261 participants. The pooled AUC was 0.891 (95% CI: 0.853-0.928), with low between-study heterogeneity ( = 29.0%, = 0.238). The bivariate random-effects model yielded a pooled sensitivity of 0.666 (95% CI: 0.578-0.744) and a pooled specificity of 0.919 (95% CI: 0.842-0.960). Exploratory subgroup analyses did not provide robust evidence supporting the superiority of any specific subgroup, and their interpretation was limited by small subgroup sizes and methodological heterogeneity. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of studies within individual subgroups. CONCLUSION: AI-driven imaging-based prediction models showed generally favorable discrimination in predicting HT after MT in AIS. However, current evidence does not establish the superiority of any specific model type. The predominance of retrospective studies, limited external validation, and methodological heterogeneity limit the generalizability of current findings. Large, multicenter prospective studies with rigorous external validation are needed before clinical implementation. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: The systematic review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261441463).

Although artificial intelligence (AI)-driven imaging-based prediction models have shown promise for predicting HT, their overall predictive performance remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated their predictive performance.

title: De-escalated rivaroxaban in postoperative isolated distal deep vein thrombosis: a propensity score-matched study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In postoperative isolated distal deep vein thrombosis (IDDVT), anticoagulation intensity is frequently constrained by bleeding risk, which may compromise treatment continuity and clinical effectiveness. OBJECTIVES: To compare the effectiveness and safety of a de-escalated (rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily) versus standard-maintenance rivaroxaban regimen for postoperative IDDVT in a real-world surgical cohort. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients diagnosed with IDDVT following urological surgery between 2013 and 2025. Patients received rivaroxaban at either a low maintenance dose (10 mg once daily) or a standard maintenance dose (20 mg once daily) according to routine clinical practice. Propensity score matching (1:1) was applied to balance baseline characteristics, incorporating surgical approach (endoscopic vs. major structural procedures) as a surrogate for surgical trauma and bleeding risk. The primary outcome was thrombus progression to proximal deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism. Secondary outcomes included IDDVT resolution and clinically relevant non-major bleeding (CRNMB). Competing-risk analyses were performed. RESULTS: P P P After matching, 152 patients were included (76 per group). Thrombus progression did not differ significantly between groups (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 1.29; 95% CI 0.48-3.46; = 0.613). No statistically significant difference in IDDVT resolution was detected between the two groups (SHR 0.93; 95% CI, 0.64-1.36; = 0.721). The low-dose regimen was associated with a significantly lower risk of CRNMB (HR 0.31; 95% CI, 0.11-0.85; = 0.023) and fewer early bleeding-related treatment interruptions. Early postoperative hematuria was more frequent in the standard-dose group. CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center retrospective cohort of patients with isolated distal deep vein thrombosis after urological surgery, low-dose rivaroxaban (10 mg once daily) was associated with a lower incidence of clinically relevant non-major bleeding than 20 mg once daily. No statistically significant differences were detected between regimens in thrombus progression or complete thrombus resolution. However, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent antithrombotic efficacy, given nonrandomized treatment allocation, residual confounding, limited sample size, and wide confidence intervals for thrombotic outcomes. The results are hypothesis-generating and support studies-preferably randomized non-inferiority trials-to determine whether dose de-escalation can provide an acceptable balance between thrombotic protection and bleeding risk in postoperative patients.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients diagnosed with IDDVT following urological surgery between 2013 and 2025.

title: Perioperative prothrombin time activity trajectories and subsequent mortality after surgical repair of acute type A aortic dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Perioperative prothrombin time activity (PTA) changes rapidly during surgical repair of acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD), but single measurements do not capture heterogeneous longitudinal patterns. We sought to identify recurring perioperative PTA trajectories, characterize their clinical context, and examine their association with subsequent all-cause mortality. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 284 adults who underwent ATAAD repair from 2021 through 2023. Group-based trajectory modeling used the last preoperative and observed postoperative day (POD) 1-7 PTA measurements. Patients required at least three observed PTA measurements for trajectory modeling. Mortality analyses began immediately after POD7. The primary Cox model adjusted for age and sex; Firth regression addressed sparse events. Incremental information beyond last preoperative PTA was evaluated by a prespecified likelihood-ratio comparison. RESULTS: P P P P P The trajectory cohort comprised 268 patients with 1,895 observations and 27 deaths after POD7. Four perioperative PTA trajectory groups were identified: moderate-stable [87 (32.5%)], low-declining [50 (18.7%)], preserved-rapidly-declining [61 (22.8%)], and high-preserved [70 (26.1%)]. Cumulative mortality differed globally (log-rank = 0.00210), and trajectory group remained associated with subsequent mortality in the age- and sex-adjusted Cox model (global = 0.0322) and Firth sensitivity analysis (global = 0.0481). The prespecified direct low-declining-versus-preserved-rapidly-declining comparison did not demonstrate a clear difference. Adding trajectory group to age, sex, and last preoperative PTA did not show clear incremental information (likelihood-ratio = 0.304; Firth = 0.380). After exclusion of mechanical-valve recipients, the principal trajectory structure was largely preserved, although this sensitivity analysis did not exclude treatment-related effects on PTA. CONCLUSION: Four reproducible perioperative PTA trajectories characterized distinct longitudinal patterns and were associated with mortality after the POD7 landmark. These trajectories should be interpreted as composite perioperative patterns reflecting both disease and treatment context rather than as intrinsic coagulation states. They were not ordered mortality-risk tiers and did not show clear incremental prognostic information beyond last preoperative PTA. External validation is required.

We sought to identify recurring perioperative PTA trajectories, characterize their clinical context, and examine their association with subsequent all-cause mortality. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 284 adults who underwent ATAAD repair from 2021 through 2023.

title: Comparison of ultrasound-guided oblique-axis versus short-axis approaches for right internal jugular vein cannulation in the left decubitus position: a prospective, randomized, single-center trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Central venous cannulation in the left decubitus position is more difficult than in the supine position and may be required when patients cannot safely return to supine. Whether the oblique-axis (OA) approach improves the success and safety of right internal jugular vein (RIJV) cannulation compared with the short-axis (SA) approach remains unknown. METHODS: Seventy-four patients (ASA I-III) scheduled for elective surgery in the left decubitus position under general anesthesia requiring RIJV cannulation were randomly assigned 1:1 to the OA or SA group (n = 37 each). Under real-time ultrasound guidance and a 20° Trendelenburg tilt, cannulation was performed by one of three experienced attending anesthesiologists, each with more than 15 years of experience in ultrasound-guided central venous cannulation. Venipuncture attempts and total procedure time were recorded by a separate investigator; patients were blinded by general anesthesia. The primary outcome was first-time puncture success; secondary outcomes were overall cannulation success, procedure time, venipuncture attempts, and mechanical complications. RESULTS: All 74 randomized patients completed the trial and were analyzed. The first-time puncture success rate was higher in the OA group (27/37 [73.0%] vs. 18/37 [48.6%]; risk difference 24.3%, 95% CI 2.8% to 45.9%; P = 0.032, Pearson chi-square test; Fisher exact test P = 0.056). Venipuncture attempts were fewer in the OA group (median 1 vs. 2; IQR 1-2; P = 0.037). Total procedure time did not differ significantly between groups (median 2.79 [IQR 2.46-3.19] vs. 3.01 [2.72-3.45] min; P = 0.060). Mechanical complications occurred in 6 of 37 patients (16.2%) in the SA group (one arterial puncture and five posterior wall penetrations) and in none in the OA group (P = 0.025); overall cannulation success was 100% in both groups. CONCLUSIONS: For RIJV cannulation in the left decubitus position, the oblique-axis approach was associated with a higher first-time puncture success rate than the short-axis approach and with fewer mechanical complications detected during or immediately after the procedure; however, the primary-endpoint evidence was borderline and the complication estimates were imprecise. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400091385; registered 28 October 2024).

title: A pilot study of the InVera Infusion Device: Twelve-month outcomes in the treatment of incompetent saphenous veins.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The InVera Infusion Device (IVID; InVera Medical) is a novel catheter designed for the delivery of sclerosant agents during nonthermal, nontumescent ablation of incompetent superficial truncal veins of the lower extremity. This device pilot study aimed to evaluate the technical success, safety, and 12-month clinical outcome. METHODS: A single-center, prospective pilot study enrolled 10 patients with primary symptomatic axial reflux who underwent chemical ablation procedures with sclerosant delivery using the IVID. Primary outcomes assessed were technical procedural success, adverse events, revised Venous Clinical Severity Score (rVCSS), patient-reported outcomes based on a Heaviness, Achiness, Swelling, Throbbing, and Itching (HASTI) symptom questionnaire, and anatomical success rates from duplex ultrasound examination at baseline, 1 and 8 weeks, 3, 6, and 12 months postprocedure. Baseline and 12-month postprocedures were compared for both the rVCSS and the HASTI results using a paired t-test and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test respectively. RESULTS: Technical procedural success was 100%. There were no device-related adverse events or serious adverse events including no deep vein thrombosis recorded throughout the follow-up period. Clinician assessed rVCSS and patient reported HASTI scores both showed statistically significant reductions from baseline to 12 months (adjusted P = .03 for both). Ultrasound-based anatomical assessment at 12 months demonstrated elimination of abnormal reflux and complete or partial occlusion in 90% of patients. CONCLUSIONS: The IVID provides a safe and effective technique for the delivery of sclerosant agents as part of the management of incompetent saphenous veins, demonstrating favorable 12-month anatomical, clinical and patient-reported outcomes in this pilot cohort.

METHODS: A single-center, prospective pilot study enrolled 10 patients with primary symptomatic axial reflux who underwent chemical ablation procedures with sclerosant delivery using the IVID.

title: Systematic review of devices, designs, and trials for the treatment of deep venous reflux.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Chronic venous insufficiency is driven primarily by venous reflux and affects nearly one-third of adults. Although superficial reflux is effectively treated with ablation, therapeutic options for deep venous reflux (DVR) remain limited. Despite decades of innovation, no prosthetic or bioprosthetic venous valve has achieved U.S. regulatory approval. We systematically reviewed device strategies, clinical and hemodynamic outcomes, complications, and barriers to translation for devices designed to treat DVR. METHODS: We conducted an International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251101761) of six databases from inception through February 2026, including in vivo animal and human studies evaluating prosthetic or bioprosthetic devices for DVR. Studies of native valve repair or autotransplantation were excluded. The primary outcome for human studies was clinical improvement, and secondary outcomes included patency, procedural complications, valvular function, and thrombosis. RESULTS: Of 516 records identified, 15 met inclusion criteria: eight human and seven animal studies. Two principal strategies were identified: intraluminal valve restoration and external compression, with approximately 40% of devices delivered percutaneously or endovenously. In human studies, technical success ranged from 87.7% to 100%, patency from 67% to 100%, and perioperative complication rates from 0% to 44%, consisting primarily of bleeding, wound infection, and valve thrombosis. Valve occlusion occurred in up to 28% of animal implants and 18% to 22% of select human cohorts. Two perioperative deaths occurred in animal studies; none were reported in human studies. Among human studies, valve competency assessment methods varied substantially. Reported competency ranged from 0% to 92%, reflecting heterogeneity in imaging modalities and definitions. Discordance between anatomic patency, duplex-derived reflux reduction, and clinical improvement was frequently observed. In contemporary multicenter trial data, fewer than half of patients met predefined reflux-reduction end points despite high device patency and substantial clinical improvement, highlighting discordance between anatomic, hemodynamic, and patient-centered outcomes. By 1 year, pain had improved in 75% to 97% of patients; revised Venous Clinical Severity Scores decreased by 37% to 81%, with clinically meaningful (≥3-point) improvement in up to 84.6%; and ulcer healing ranged from 67% to 100%. Longer follow-up extended to 2 years in animal studies and up to 11 years in human series with various outcomes reported. CONCLUSIONS: Several devices developed for DVR have demonstrated technical feasibility and symptom improvement. However, the risk of thrombosis, the marginal impact on valvular function, and the lack of standardization and selection of adequate end points in the measurement of results remain major barriers to regulatory approval. Standardized composite end points integrating objective hemodynamic measures with patient-centered outcomes are essential to advance durable DVR device development and clinical translation.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear. METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows. DISCUSSION: In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.

title: Comparative outcomes of arteriovenous accesses with and without tunneled hemodialysis catheters: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: This study compared patency rates of arteriovenous accesses with and without concurrent tunneled hemodialysis catheter (THC) use, addressing limited research on combined outcomes. A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted on patients undergoing arteriovenous access creation at a single hospital between January 2021 and December 2022. Primary outcomes were the 6-month primary patency rate and functional dialysis success. Secondary outcomes were the factors associated with each of these endpoints. Statistical analyses employed t tests, chi-square tests, logistic regression, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves. A total of 319 vascular accesses were included. The 6-month patency rate was significantly higher in the access-only group than in the access + THC group (87.04% vs 78.20%, P = .04). THC usage (odds ratio [OR] = 0.49, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.25-0.95, P = .03), graft usage (OR = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.18-0.82, P = .01), and higher hemoglobin levels (OR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.65-0.96, P = .02) were associated with reduced patency rates. Functional dialysis success at 6 months did not differ significantly between groups (87.96% vs 83.89%, P = .21). However, older age (OR = 0.96, 95% CI: 0.93-0.99, P = .01), use of a cubital artery to an autologous vein (OR = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.19-0.82, P = .01) or graft (OR = 0.40, 95% CI: 0.17-0.97, P = .04), and higher hemoglobin levels (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.66-0.99, P = .03) were associated with a lower likelihood of functional dialysis success. Concurrent THC use was independently associated with reduced 6-month primary patency without a corresponding reduction in the short-term delivery of dialysis, suggesting an increased need for interventions to maintain the access. Judicious use of THCs and careful consideration of the vascular access type are important to optimize vascular access outcomes in patients undergoing hemodialysis.

Primary outcomes were the 6-month primary patency rate and functional dialysis success.

title: Apparent Diffusion Coefficient Composition and Tissue Heterogeneity as Predictors of Functional Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Patients With Large Ischemic Core.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Recent trials established endovascular thrombectomy efficacy in large ischemic cores, yet outcomes remain heterogeneous despite similar infarct volumes, suggesting that current volumetric assessments may not fully capture tissue viability. We examined whether tissue composition quantified by apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) distribution and tissue heterogeneity within baseline diffusion-weighted imaging lesions are associated with functional outcomes in large-core patients after successful endovascular thrombectomy. METHODS: -6 2 We retrospectively analyzed patients with large vessel occlusion with large ischemic cores (diffusion-weighted imaging candidate volume ≥50 mL) achieving successful reperfusion after endovascular thrombectomy. We quantified ADC tissue composition as proportions within 3 ADC ranges relative to total diffusion-weighted imaging lesion volume: low (<540), mid (540-700), and high (>700 × 10mm/s). Separately, tissue heterogeneity was assessed using Shannon entropy, a metric quantifying ADC distribution heterogeneity. The primary outcome was 3-month good functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score of 0-3), analyzed via adjusted logistic regression. RESULTS: P P Among 126 patients (age, 70.8±12.4 years; 60.3% men; diffusion-weighted imaging candidate volume, 93.7±41.2 mL), 39.7% achieved a good functional outcome. Both tissue heterogeneity (adjusted odds ratio, 1.45 per 0.1-unit increase, 1.09-1.93,=0.011, area under the curve, 0.671) and mid-ADC fraction (adjusted odds ratio, 1.78 per 5% increase, 1.20-2.63,=0.004, area under the curve, 0.688) were associated with good functional outcomes. Neither low-ADC nor high-ADC fractions showed significant associations with functional outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: -6 2 Higher mid-ADC (540-700 × 10mm/s) fraction and greater tissue heterogeneity predicted favorable outcomes in patients with large ischemic core, indicating that tissue composition within the ischemic core, beyond its volume, is associated with functional outcome after reperfusion. Among large-core patients who achieved successful reperfusion, ADC-based tissue characterization may help predict functional outcome.

title: Optimizing Vessel Preparation in Femoropopliteal Lesions: Does the Chocolate Balloon Deliver on Its Clinical Promise?
abstract: The "leave nothing behind" paradigm using drug-coated balloons (DCBs) has reshaped femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease treatment, though clinical success remains heavily contingent upon optimal vessel preparation. In a recent issue of The American Journal of Cardiology, Li and colleagues address the limitations of conventional plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA) through a propensity score-matched analysis of 508 patients from the multicenter PROMISING registry, comparing specialized vessel preparation using the nitinol-constrained Chocolate balloon against POBA before DCB angioplasty. The Chocolate balloon significantly reduced the primary endpoint of bailout stenting (20.47% vs 29.92%) and facilitated larger final DCB diameters, though these acute mechanical advantages did not translate into statistically significant differences in clinical outcomes at 12 months. This commentary examines this striking "procedural-to-clinical paradox," highlighting how the potent antiproliferative effect of DCBs and the acute compensatory function of bailout stents may temporarily mask early clinical divergence. Given that cumulative mechanical failures of permanent metallic implants typically emerge beyond one year in hostile biomechanical environments, longer-term observation remains essential to capture the true clinical dividend of a stent-free strategy.

title: Outcomes of hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation (HEPATIC): an international, multicentre, retrospective registry study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is a severe complication that can lead to acute graft failure, often requiring urgent re-transplantation. We aimed to assess the 1-year incidence of graft loss and mortality and to evaluate outcomes according to the timing of hepatic artery thrombosis and the treatment approaches in patients with hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation. METHODS: In this international, multicentre, retrospective study, the HEPATIC registry, which had 33 centres across 21 countries as of December, 2025, was used to identify patients who developed hepatic artery thrombosis at age younger than 18 years after paediatric liver transplantation between Jan 1, 2002, and Dec 31, 2021, and who either received a diagnosis of or received an intervention for hepatic artery thrombosis before Jan 1, 2023. Donor-related, recipient-related, and transplantation-related characteristics collected from local medical records were entered retrospectively into electronic case reports by participating centres, with centralised data quality control. Primary outcomes were 1-year graft loss and mortality after hepatic artery thrombosis diagnosis. The outcomes were examined based on when hepatic artery thrombosis occurred after paediatric liver transplantation (early [≤7 days] vs late [>7 days]), primary management strategy (conservative management, surgical revascularisation, endovascular therapy, or immediate listing for re-transplantation), and transplantation era (in 5-year intervals). The registry was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05818644. FINDINGS: Hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 415 patients, of whom 216 (52%) were female and 199 (48%) were male, and median age was 1·7 years (IQR 0·8-6·5). Median follow-up was 50·9 months (IQR 17·0-112·6). Graft loss occurred in 180 patients by 1 month (cumulative incidence 43% [95% CI 38-48]) and 222 by 1 year (54% [49-58]); 51 patients died by 1 month (12% [9-15]) and 77 by 1 year (19% [15-22]). Surgical revascularisation was the first-line treatment approach in 195 (47%) patients. Other strategies included listing for re-transplantation in 99 (24%), conservative management in 79 (19%), and endovascular therapy in 42 (10%). Treatment approaches changed over time, with increased use of conservative management and endovascular therapy and reduced listing for re-transplantation (p<0·0001), with no accompanying change in 1-year mortality across eras (p=0·14). Early (≤7 days) hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 282 (68%) patients and was associated with higher 1-year graft loss than late (>7 days) hepatic artery thrombosis (cumulative incidence 57% [95% CI 51-63] vs 47% [37-55], log-rank p=0·010). Surgical revascularisation was used in 167 (59%) patients and listing for re-transplantation in 66 (23%) patients with early hepatic artery thrombosis, whereas conservative management was used in 51 (38%) patients and endovascular therapy in 21 (16%) patients with late hepatic artery thrombosis; however, 1-year mortality did not differ between treatment strategies among patients with early versus late hepatic artery thrombosis. INTERPRETATION: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is associated with notably high 1-year graft loss and mortality, particularly if hepatic artery thrombosis occurs within 7 days after the procedure. The management strategies for hepatic artery thrombosis differ according to the post-transplantation timing of hepatic artery thrombosis occurrence. Despite changes in management over the past 20 years, outcomes have remained poor, underscoring the need to improve therapeutic strategies for this complication. FUNDING: None.

title: Long-term graft and patient survival of patients with portal vein stenosis after pediatric liver transplantation: Results from the multicenter multinational PORTAL registry.
abstract: Pediatric liver transplantation (pLT) has become a standard treatment, but it is still burdened by complications such as portal vein stenosis (PVS). PVS can result in compromised graft function and portal hypertension if left untreated. We aimed to assess long-term patient and graft survival after PVS diagnosis following pLT. Our study analyzed data from the Portal Vein Obstruction Revascularisation Therapy After Liver Transplantation (PORTAL) registry, which contains retrospective data from 21 centers across 18 countries, over a 20-year period. Graft and patient survival rates were determined after PVS diagnosis. This study included 239 patients (53% female; median age at pLT 1.1   y) diagnosed with PVS. The median age at diagnosis was 2.7 years. The overall 10-year graft survival was 90%, and the 10-year patient survival was 96%. One-year graft and patient survival were lowest in patients with PVS diagnosed ≤7 days after pLT (80% and 92%, respectively). Initial treatment strategies comprised mostly endovascular procedures (87%), followed by conservative (11%) and surgical treatment (3%). Patient outcomes did not differ between these treatment groups. Within the endovascular group, graft survival in patients treated with stent (n=26) was significantly lower compared with those with percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (n=181) (88% vs. 98%, respectively, p =0.01). Our findings indicate excellent graft and patient survival after PVS diagnosis and its treatment. Further research is needed to determine the safety and efficacy of optimal management strategies, especially in early-onset PVS.

PVS can result in compromised graft function and portal hypertension if left untreated. We aimed to assess long-term patient and graft survival after PVS diagnosis following pLT.

title: "Not so Minor" - Digital Amputation as a Precursor to Major Amputation and Mortality in an Irish Tertiary Vascular Center.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Minor (toe) amputations are a common consequence of peripheral arterial disease and/or diabetes. They can herald further forefoot and major amputations and are a poor prognostic indicator for 5-year survival. This study aimed to identify prognostic indicators for progression from minor amputation to major amputation and all-cause mortality. METHODS: Index digital amputations performed by vascular surgeons in a tertiary referral hospital between 2017 and 2022 were identified from Hospital In-Patient Enquiry data. Electronic records for each limb were followed up to October 2025 for further ipsilateral minor and major amputations and mortality. RESULTS: A total of 224 limbs in 209 patients underwent at least 1 minor amputation. The cohort was predominantly male (86%) with a mean age of 66.3 years (±12.7). 70% had peripheral arterial disease and 80% had diabetes. In total, 34% (n = 73/215) required further ipsilateral amputation, 78.3% of which occurred within 12 months of index surgery. Minor and major reamputation rates were 25.6% and 11%, respectively. Predictors of further amputation at any level included ischemic heart disease (IHD) (odds ratio [OR] 2.796, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.54-5.06), diabetes (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.04-5.136), and dialysis (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.021-4.915). Index hallux amputation, IHD, and revascularization at index admission were risk factors for further major ipsilateral amputation. All-cause mortality was 11.4%, 24.8%, and 48% at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. CONCLUSION: Consistent with international data, minor amputations are poor prognostic factor for limb loss and death. In this cohort, patients with IHD and dialysis were most at risk for further amputation.

They can herald further forefoot and major amputations and are a poor prognostic indicator for 5-year survival. This study aimed to identify prognostic indicators for progression from minor amputation to major amputation and all-cause mortality.

title: Comparative Outcomes of Endovascular and Open Surgical Repair for Extracranial Carotid Artery Aneurysms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Extracranial carotid artery aneurysms (ECAAs) are rare lesions managed by open surgical repair (OpR) or endovascular repair (ER). We compared the perioperative and long-term outcomes of both strategies. METHODS: A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA)-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis, registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO), was performed. Comparative studies were pooled using random-effects models, and separate single-arm meta-analyses were conducted for OpR and ER. RESULTS: Twenty-six retrospective studies involving 707 patients and 725 procedures were included (574 OpR and 151 ER). Six comparative studies (228 procedures) showed no significant differences between ER and OpR in 30-day mortality (odds ratio [OR], 2.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.53-12.52), 30-day stroke (OR, 1.08; 95% CI, 0.30-3.91), late stroke, reintervention, or primary patency. In the single-arm analyses, pooled 30-day mortality and stroke rates after OpR were 1.18% and 4.29%, respectively. No 30-day deaths and one stroke were reported after ER, yielding a pooled stroke rate of 1.25% (95% CI, 0.18-8.34). Primary patency was high after both OpR (98.44%) and ER (94.50%). CONCLUSION: Observational evidence suggests similar perioperative outcomes and similar observed late event rates for ER and OpR in ECAAs, although heterogeneous follow up and the absence of time-to-event analyses limit formal comparison of long-term durability. Both approaches were associated with low mortality, stroke, reintervention rates, and excellent primary patency. Open repair remains supported by a larger body of evidence and longer follow up, whereas evidence for ER remains comparatively limited. Because treatment allocation in the available studies was influenced by patient characteristics, anatomical complexity, and surgical risk, the observed similarity in outcomes should not be interpreted as evidence of therapeutic equivalence. Given the observational design and the predominantly moderate-to-serious risk of bias of the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Extracranial carotid artery aneurysms (ECAAs) are rare lesions managed by open surgical repair (OpR) or endovascular repair (ER). We compared the perioperative and long-term outcomes of both strategies. METHODS: A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA)-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis, registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO), was performed.

title: Endovascular Iliac Stenting Versus Open Aortobifemoral Bypass for Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease: A Retrospective Multicentre Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortoiliac occlusive disease (AIOD) causing chronic or critical limb-threatening ischemia can be treated by open aortobifemoral bypass (ABF) or endovascular reconstruction. Comparative effectiveness data adjusted for treatment selection bias remain limited. This multicenter study compared mid-term outcomes of endovascular versus open reconstruction for AIOD. METHODS: Retrospective, nonrandomized cohort study of 171 patients with AIOD (Rutherford 3-6) treated at three centers (UK, Ireland, and Egypt) between January 2023 and February 2026. Outcomes were primary patency, freedom from reintervention (FFR), amputation-free survival (AFS), overall survival, and perioperative complications. Cox regression and inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to adjust for confounding. RESULTS: 125 patients (73.1%) underwent endovascular treatment and 46 (26.9%) open bypass. Endovascular patients were older (66.8 vs 60.8 years, P < 0.001) and had a lower burden of TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus II (TASC II) C-D disease (53.6% vs 93.5%, P < 0.001). Primary patency at 24 months was 62.7% versus 91.8% (log-rank P < 0.001; IPTW-adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 5.67, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.75-18.37). FFR at 24 months was 63.1% versus 93.3% (P < 0.001). AFS (85.0% vs 87.4%, P = 0.992) and overall survival (93.3% vs 90.0%, P = 0.335) were comparable between groups. Wound infection was less frequent after endovascular treatment (0.8% vs 10.9%, P = 0.006). Major amputation was independently predicted by critical limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) presentation (odds ratio [OR] 4.0) and age, not treatment group. Progressive infrainguinal disease, rather than failure of proximal revascularization, accounted for most amputations in both groups. CONCLUSION: Open bypass confers a substantial mid-term patency and reintervention-free survival advantage over endovascular reconstruction for AIOD, most pronounced in TASC D and CLTI subgroups, without a corresponding difference in limb salvage or survival. These findings support risk-stratified rather than uniformly endovascular-first treatment selection, pending confirmation from the ongoing Endovascular Versus Open revascularisation in severe oCClusive aorto-iliac disease (EVOCC) randomized trial.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Aortoiliac occlusive disease (AIOD) causing chronic or critical limb-threatening ischemia can be treated by open aortobifemoral bypass (ABF) or endovascular reconstruction. Comparative effectiveness data adjusted for treatment selection bias remain limited. This multicenter study compared mid-term outcomes of endovascular versus open reconstruction for AIOD.

title: Distinct Temporal Patterns of Limb Loss and Mortality after Transcatheter Arterialization of the Deep Veins for No-Option CLTI.
abstract: BACKGROUND: No-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) represents the most advanced stage of peripheral arterial disease, characterized by exhausted revascularization options and substantial systemic comorbidity. Contemporary registry data have reported amputation-free survival (AFS) as low as approximately 37% at 1 year with standard care alone. Deep venous arterialization has emerged as a limb-salvage strategy for these patients by arterializing the venous circulation to restore perfusion to the distal extremity. Although early trial data have been encouraging, the durability of transcatheter arterialization of the deep veins (TADV) in routine clinical practice beyond the trial setting remains incompletely defined. We evaluated 2-year technical and clinical outcomes following TADV in a single-center cohort. METHODS: We performed a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 29 consecutive patients with no-option CLTI who underwent TADV, with follow-up extending up to 2 years. Outcomes assessed included technical success, 30-day circuit patency, major amputation, limb salvage, all-cause mortality, and AFS. Kaplan-Meier methods were used to estimate time-to-event outcomes, and univariable Cox regression was used to identify baseline factors associated with AFS and mortality. RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in all 29 patients (100%). During the follow-up, limb salvage was maintained in 22 of 29 patients (75.9%). The Kaplan-Meier limb-salvage curve plateaued after approximately 7 months, with no major amputations observed among patients who remained amputation-free beyond this point. All-cause mortality was 41.4% (12 of 29 patients) and increased throughout follow-up (Table 2). Older age was significantly associated with mortality (median, 77 vs. 71 years; P = 0.047), and congestive heart failure showed a nonsignificant trend toward increased mortality risk (83.3% vs. 47.1%; P = 0.064). CONCLUSION: In this cohort of patients with no-option CLTI, TADV achieved durable limb preservation in approximately three-quarters of patients through 2 years of follow-up, with amputation occurring almost exclusively within the first several months after the procedure. All-cause mortality remained substantial throughout follow-up, consistent with the comorbidity burden of this population. These findings support TADV as a limb-salvage option for patients with no-option CLTI who would otherwise face major amputation, although larger multicenter studies are needed to confirm long-term durability.

Contemporary registry data have reported amputation-free survival (AFS) as low as approximately 37% at 1 year with standard care alone. Deep venous arterialization has emerged as a limb-salvage strategy for these patients by arterializing the venous circulation to restore perfusion to the distal extremity.

title: Association between Increased Superficial Calcification Clusters in Carotid Atherosclerosis and Cardiovascular Events after Carotid Artery Stenting: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The role of calcification in carotid atherosclerosis before and after carotid artery stenting (CAS) remains controversial. This study assessed the association between the extent of calcification in target carotid plaques and outcomes after CAS. METHODS: A total of 292 subjects with carotid stenosis who underwent CAS were retrospectively enrolled. Follow-up for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) was conducted via outpatient visits and telephone. Ultimately, 211 subjects completed 2-year follow-up. Superficial calcification clusters were counted on computed tomography angiography. Subjects with ≥4 superficial calcification clusters (n = 24) were matched in a 1:4 ratio to those with <4 superficial calcification clusters (n = 96). Sensitivity analysis was performed based on the matched cohort. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 1.92 years, 14 MACEs occurring more than 30 days after discharge were recorded. In univariate Cox analysis, symptom status (P = 0.0116), alcohol abuse (P = 0.0091), total number of calcification clusters (P = 0.0428), and number of superficial calcification clusters (P = 0.0022) were significantly associated with MACEs. In bivariate analyses, the number of superficial calcification clusters maintained a reasonably good association with MACEs. In sensitivity analysis, superficial calcification clusters remained significantly associated with MACE when loss to follow-up was classified as MACE (P = 0.0256, HR = 1.2548, 95% CI 1.0281-1.5315) or as no MACE (P = 0.0265, HR = 1.4948, 95% CI 1.0479-2.1323). CONCLUSION: The number of superficial calcification clusters may independently serve as a prognostic risk factor in patients with carotid atherosclerosis undergoing CAS.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The role of calcification in carotid atherosclerosis before and after carotid artery stenting (CAS) remains controversial. This study assessed the association between the extent of calcification in target carotid plaques and outcomes after CAS. METHODS: A total of 292 subjects with carotid stenosis who underwent CAS were retrospectively enrolled.
